context.pr_body:
I haven't removed the stuff that's ``model_selection`` now, in case we want to give that another version.
Also some other stuff still needs to be done.

Remove code tagged to be removed in v.0.20. Stole todo from #10094

Things to remove:
* Classes (reported [here](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/effd75dda5f4afa61f988035ff8fe4b3a447464e/doc/modules/classes.rst#L1405))
   - [x] cross_validation.KFold
   - [x] cross_validation.LabelKFold
   - [x] cross_validation.LeaveOneLabelOut
   - [x] cross_validation.LeaveOneOut
   - [x] cross_validation.LeavePOut
   - [x] cross_validation.LeavePLabelOut
   - [x] cross_validation.LabelShuffleSplit
   - [x] cross_validation.ShuffleSplit
   - [x] cross_validation.StratifiedKFold
   - [x] cross_validation.StratifiedShuffleSplit
   - [x] cross_validation.PredefinedSplit
   - [x] decomposition.RandomizedPCA
   - [x] gaussian_process.GaussianProcess
   - [x] grid_search.ParameterGrid
   - [x] grid_search.ParameterSampler
   - [x] grid_search.GridSearchCV
   - [x] grid_search.RandomizedSearchCV
   - [x] mixture.DPGMM
   - [x] mixture.GMM
   - [x] mixture.VBGMM



* from whats new reported [here](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/master/doc/whats_new/v0.18.rst#api-changes-summary-1)
    * Linear, kernelized and related models
    
       - [x] ``residual_metric`` has been deprecated in :class:`linear_model.RANSACRegressor`. Use ``loss`` instead. By `Manoj Kumar`_.
       - [ ] Access to public attributes ``.X_`` and ``.y_`` has been deprecated in :class:`isotonic.IsotonicRegression`. By :user:`Jonathan Arfa <jarfa>`.
    
    * Decomposition, manifold learning and clustering
    
       - [x] The old :class:`mixture.DPGMM` is deprecated in favor of the new :class:`mixture.BayesianGaussianMixture` (with the parameter ``weight_concentration_prior_type='dirichlet_process'``). The new class solves the computational problems of the old class and computes the Gaussian mixture with a Dirichlet process prior faster than before. :issue:`7295` by :user:`Wei Xue <xuewei4d>` and :user:`Thierry Guillemot <tguillemot>`.
       - [x] The old :class:`mixture.VBGMM` is deprecated in favor of the new :class:`mixture.BayesianGaussianMixture` (with the parameter ``weight_concentration_prior_type='dirichlet_distribution'``). The new class solves the computational problems of the old class and computes the Variational Bayesian Gaussian mixture faster than before. :issue:`6651` by :user:`Wei Xue <xuewei4d>` and :user:`Thierry Guillemot <tguillemot>`.
       - [x] The old :class:`mixture.GMM` is deprecated in favor of the new :class:`mixture.GaussianMixture`. The new class computes the Gaussian mixture faster than before and some of computational problems have been solved. :issue:`6666` by :user:`Wei Xue <xuewei4d>` and :user:`Thierry Guillemot <tguillemot>`.
    
    * Model evaluation and meta-estimators
    
       - [x] The :mod:`sklearn.cross_validation`, :mod:`sklearn.grid_search` and :mod:`sklearn.learning_curve` have been deprecated and the classes and functions have been reorganized into the :mod:`sklearn.model_selection` module. Ref :ref:`model_selection_changes` for more information. :issue:`4294` by `Raghav RV`_.
    
       - [x] The ``grid_scores_`` attribute of :class:`model_selection.GridSearchCV` and :class:`model_selection.RandomizedSearchCV` is deprecated in favor of the attribute ``cv_results_``. Ref :ref:`model_selection_changes` for more information. :issue:`6697` by `Raghav RV`_.
       - [x] The parameters ``n_iter`` or ``n_folds`` in old CV splitters are replaced by the new parameter ``n_splits`` since it can provide a consistent and unambiguous interface to represent the number of train-test splits. :issue:`7187` by :user:`YenChen Lin <yenchenlin>`.
       - [x] ``classes`` parameter was renamed to ``labels`` in :func:`metrics.hamming_loss`. :issue:`7260` by :user:`Sebastián Vanrell <srvanrell>`.
       - [x] The splitter classes ``LabelKFold``, ``LabelShuffleSplit``, ``LeaveOneLabelOut`` and ``LeavePLabelsOut`` are renamed to :class:`model_selection.GroupKFold`, :class:`model_selection.GroupShuffleSplit`, :class:`model_selection.LeaveOneGroupOut` and :class:`model_selection.LeavePGroupsOut` respectively. Also the parameter ``labels`` in the :func:`split` method of the newly renamed splitters :class:`model_selection.LeaveOneGroupOut` and :class:`model_selection.LeavePGroupsOut` is renamed to ``groups``. Additionally in :class:`model_selection.LeavePGroupsOut`, the parameter ``n_labels`` is renamed to ``n_groups``. :issue:`6660` by `Raghav RV`_.
       - [x] Error and loss names for ``scoring`` parameters are now prefixed by ``'neg_'``, such as ``neg_mean_squared_error``. The unprefixed versions are deprecated and will be removed in version 0.20. :issue:`7261` by :user:`Tim Head <betatim>`.

## files with remaining deprecated lines

context.pr_title: Studio: per-account isolation for shared installs and the desktop app
context.pr_body:
## Summary

Studio and the desktop app can be shared by several people on one machine. The installation owner (the existing `unsloth` login) creates accounts from Settings > Accounts. Each account signs in with a one-time setup code, sets a password, and then has its own chats, projects, settings, credentials, uploads, datasets, training runs, outputs, exports, galleries, RAG store, sandboxes and temporary files. Nothing an account does is visible to, or can affect, another account.

A single-account install is unchanged: same paths, same database files, same password-only login, same desktop auto-login, same keyless loopback behaviour, and no extra I/O on the hot paths. Multi-account policy switches on only when a second account exists.

## How isolation works

- Identity is an immutable `account_id`; usernames are display names only, so re-creating a username never inherits data.
- Each request is bound to its account through a `ContextVar`; storage roots, database paths and caches resolve through it at call time. Background work carries the account explicitly, and unbound work resolves to the owner.
- Managed accounts live under `<studio home>/accounts/<account_id>/`; the owner stays at the legacy root. The model cache, binaries, the auth database and the Hugging Face cache are shared, and a managed account sees a cached model only when it is provably public or it downloaded it.
- Every storage module initialises its schema per database path. Paths must resolve inside the account's own roots, including through symlinks.
- Object routes answer 404 for another account's ids. Deactivating an account invalidates its tokens and API keys; deleting it cancels its jobs, closes its MCP sessions and renames its roots aside, all or nothing.
- Preview and RAG download links are bound to the minting account. Model load and unload rows in the API monitor are visible only to the owner and the loading account.
- Installation-wide actions (accounts, updates, installers, shutdown, executables, caches, network settings) are owner-only.

## Login, reset, desktop, downgrade

- `/api/auth/status` reports `login_mode` and never lists accounts. With one account the form is unchanged; with more, a username field appears and the setup code is the first password.
- `unsloth studio reset-password` keeps its behaviour for one account and requires `--username` with several.
- The desktop shell still starts and adopts the backend with its secret and authenticates its ownership probe and quit path with that secret. With one account it auto-signs in; with several it shows the login form.
- After a downgrade a managed account gets 401 everywhere instead of the owner's data; the next upgrade brings it back. `full_access` stays off while any managed account record exists.

## Sandboxes and the shared GPU

- Sandboxes are per account. Full tool access is refused server-side whenever more than one account exists. A managed account's python and terminal tool processes are confined at the OS level (Landlock ABI 6 on Linux 6.12 or later, which also keeps signals inside the tool's own process tree, `sandbox-exec` on macOS): read-only workspace, no link creation, and the install root, other accounts' roots, the shared Hugging Face cache and the per-user temp tree are hidden. Where no mechanism exists, code execution is refused for managed accounts; the owner can opt out with `UNSLOTH_STUDIO_ALLOW_UNCONFINED_TOOLS=1`.
- GPU arbitration is ownership-aware: a different model while another account is generating is refused with 409 `gpu_busy` and `Retry-After`; an idle swap happens as today. Cancel is scoped to the caller and rechecked under the engine lock. Another account's resident model reports `{"loaded": true, "yours": false}` (the chat status keeps its list shape: `{"loaded": [], "loading": [], "yours": false}`).
- Same model, same settings: a load that matches the resident chat model reuses it instead of evicting and relaunching llama-server, and the account joins its sharers. Every sharer sees and uses the model from Studio and the OpenAI routes; chats, cancels, monitor rows and credentials stay per account. A sharer's unload drops only its share while others remain; the last sharer or the installation owner tears the model down. A replacement load, teardown, idle unload, deactivation or deletion resets the shares.
- Under `--secure`, one Cloudflare quick tunnel URL serves every account with Studio's own authentication; keyless access is never admitted on the tunnel and, once a second account exists, not on loopback either.

Kept as design: the installation owner can see and unload a managed account's idle resident model and can browse its private model folder by absolute path, because the owner administers the machine.

## Verification

- Backend suite on this branch merged with main: 42,713 passed; the remaining failures are the same on main (accelerator-dependent tests and one timing test).
- Frontend: unit tests, `tsc`, strict locale parity for the Accounts strings, build and bundle budget.
- Recorded simulations: legacy install upgrade and downgrade; two-account downgrade; password reset; two accounts on one B200 with real llama-server (shared model, refused swap while streaming, idle swap, scoped cancel, delete mid-stream); parallel throughput parity with main; a real quick tunnel run; the account-switch journey on Chromium, Chrome, Edge, Firefox and WebKit; hot-path connection, query and mkdir counts identical to the merge base; a route matrix over every object route with owner, right account, wrong account, unauthenticated and deactivated actors.
- Rust unit tests for the desktop ownership probe pass locally and in the Tauri CI job.
- Single-user cost: with accounts off, every owner request runs the same sqlite connections, mkdirs and thread hops as the merge base and fewer statements (the auth schema check is cached per connection), and the counts do not change with 1, 2, 3 or 100 accounts; the account count is never re-read from auth.db on a request, no sharer or fence state is allocated on an owner-only install, and the llama admission queue is the same object for every account. Locked in by `tests/multi_account/test_routing_invariance.py`. On a B200 with Qwen3-0.6B Q4_K_M, three paired rounds of merge base versus this branch with accounts off: server decode 1768 vs 1774 tokens/s, TTFT 68.2 vs 68.8 ms, status/models/auth/threads p95 within 4 percent, load time no slower. The owner's numbers are unchanged with one idle managed account (created or logged in and polling) and with 100 accounts and 10 idle sessions; the run-to-run spread of the server-reported decode rate on this model is about 8 percent, and every scenario sits inside it.
- The multi-account browser flow is a Python Playwright driver (`tests/studio/playwright_multi_account.py`), matching the other `tests/studio/playwright_*.py` checks, so the frontend lockfile gains no new dependency.

## Relation to #10102 and #10250

This is a from-scratch implementation on today's main; #10102 and #10250 were used as references for coverage and no code was taken from them. It differs in keying storage on an immutable account id rather than the username, initialising schemas per database path, binding requests through a `ContextVar` with an async form, arbitrating the GPU instead of evicting other users' streams, refusing full access server-side, confining tool processes at the OS level, and fencing managed credentials from older builds. The four review P1s on #10250 are addressed here by construction, so #10250 can be closed in favour of this PR.

## Screenshots

Each pair is the same scene captured twice: BEFORE is the merge base, AFTER is this branch, driven against two isolated installs.

### Turning on multi-user accounts

Nothing changes until the installation owner asks for it. Sign in as the owner, open Settings, and pick the new Accounts tab. Type a username, press Create account, and that first managed account is what switches the install to multi-user. The tab, and everything on it, is owner-only: a managed account never sees it.

Studio shows the new account's setup code once. Copy it and hand it to the person it belongs to. It is their first password, it works once, and it expires in 60 minutes.

![Settings, Accounts tab: create an account and copy its setup code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielhanchen/unsloth-staging-2/pr-screenshots-10588/pr-screenshots/pr10588/v2/settings-accounts.png)

The settings search finds the tab by name, so the owner does not have to know where it lives.

![Settings search for Accounts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielhanchen/unsloth-staging-2/pr-screenshots-10588/pr-screenshots/pr10588/v2/settings-search.png)

### The account holder's first sign-in

Once a second account exists, the login form grows a Username field and says where the setup code comes from. With a single account it stays the password-only form it has always been.

![Login form gains a username field](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielhanchen/unsloth-staging-2/pr-screenshots-10588/pr-screenshots/pr10588/v2/login-form.png)

Signing in with a setup code lands on a forced password change instead of the chat, so a code that was sent over chat or email never becomes a lasting credential.

![First sign-in forces a password change](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielhanchen/unsloth-staging-2/pr-screenshots-10588/pr-screenshots/pr10588/v2/first-sign-in.png)

### Administering an account

Regenerating a setup code is the password reset path. It replaces the password, signs the account out and revokes its API keys, and the dialog says so before it happens.

![Regenerate setup code confirmation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielhanchen/unsloth-staging-2/pr-screenshots-10588/pr-screenshots/pr10588/v2/regenerate-dialog.png)

Deactivating keeps the account and its data but invalidates its tokens and API keys, and the row offers Reactivate. Deleting is the destructive one: it cancels the account's jobs, closes its MCP sessions and renames its roots aside.

![A deactivated account offers Reactivate](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielhanchen/unsloth-staging-2/pr-screenshots-10588/pr-screenshots/pr10588/v2/deactivated-row.png)

### What a managed account cannot do

Full tool access is refused server-side whenever more than one account exists, so the chat permission menu drops the Full access option for a managed account rather than offering something the backend will reject.

![Permission menu without Full access](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielhanchen/unsloth-staging-2/pr-screenshots-10588/pr-screenshots/pr10588/v2/permission-menu.png)

review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Isolate managed tool processes from private networks**

For a managed account on macOS this explicitly permits every network operation, while the Linux Landlock rules likewise leave `handled_access_net` at zero. The command checks are not a security boundary: an account can write a Python/C helper as a file and execute it after approving the tool call, allowing a remote Studio user to connect from the host to loopback, link-local metadata endpoints, or otherwise inaccessible LAN services. Managed tool processes need OS-level private-network isolation or a mediated public-only transport, as is already done for managed MCP connections.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
review_comments.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]

review_comments.body: Not a defect this PR introduces. Tool processes have run in the host network namespace since before this change (tools.py records why CLONE_NEWNET is not applied), and the confinement added here is a filesystem boundary by contract. Landlock rules are per TCP port and sandbox-exec has no address ranges, so neither can express deny-private-allow-public; a filtering proxy plus a network namespace is a separate feature that applies equally to the owner sandbox on main.
review_comments.author: danielhanchen

review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Hide sibling process environments from managed tools**

On Linux, granting the confined process read access to all of `/proc` exposes `/proc/<pid>/environ` for dumpable same-UID sibling processes. For example, model-download workers are launched with the initiating account's `HF_TOKEN` in their environment, so a managed tool running concurrently can enumerate processes and recover another account's token; hardening only the Studio parent does not protect these workers. Exclude sensitive procfs entries or otherwise isolate process visibility at the OS boundary.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
review_comments.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]

review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Confine managed job workers before loading remote code**

When a managed account enables `trust_remote_code` for a model it controls, the training/export worker eventually executes that repository's Python in this child without any filesystem confinement. The selective environment cleanup does not change the process UID, working directory, or `HOME`, so that code can enumerate and read the owner's workspace, other accounts' roots, saved host credentials, and any unlisted secret environment variables. Run managed job children inside the same account filesystem boundary used for tools, rather than relying only on validated configuration paths.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
review_comments.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]

review_comments.body: A managed account cannot enable remote code on any job path: the consent gate refuses it before the scan for every non-owner context, job children are bound to the account through run_account_child, and the only auto-enables require a Hub-verified unsloth or nvidia repo. Confining the training process itself is a separate feature, since it must read the shared cache, write outputs and load CUDA libraries.
review_comments.author: danielhanchen

review_comments.body: Landlock already denies this. /proc/<pid>/environ is gated by a ptrace access check, not by the /proc read grant, and a confined tool's domain is never a superset of an unconfined worker's, so the read fails with EACCES while cmdline still succeeds. Reproduced on this host: a sibling with HF_TOKEN in its environment, read from a confined managed tool, gives Permission denied. A preexec PR_SET_DUMPABLE is also wiped by the following execve, so the proposed fix would not work.
review_comments.author: danielhanchen

review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Authorize managed dataset downloads before using the shared cache**

For a managed account this strips ambient credentials but never verifies access to the requested dataset, unlike `download_model_response()`, which calls `authorize_download()` before consulting the shared cache. The dataset worker deliberately treats a metadata authorization failure as non-fatal, and `snapshot_download()` can return an already-complete cached snapshot; completion then records a dataset grant for the caller. Thus, naming another account's cached private dataset can convert that shared cache entry into the caller's authorized dataset without valid credentials. Call `authorize_download(repo_id, "dataset", hf_token)` before cache canonicalization or claiming the job.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
review_comments.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]

review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recheck account retirement after claiming a dataset download**

If account deletion occurs while this request is awaiting case resolution or transport selection, retirement scans the account registry before any job has been claimed and therefore completes without cancelling it. The request can then claim the dataset job here and launch a worker with the account's supplied token even though the account and its roots have already been retired. The model-download path closes the same race by calling `require_live_account()` immediately after recording ownership; the dataset path needs the same post-claim fence before clearing markers or spawning.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
review_comments.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]

review_comments.body: The post-claim fence already sits in the shared launch_worker the dataset route calls: for any account-scoped caller it records ownership and calls require_live_account before spawn, and ownership is recorded at the claim since the last round. Probes parked right after the claim and right before launch both end with 403 and no worker; a retirement landing between the two adjacent lines fails closed and keeps the roots. The model route only hoists the same idempotent check a few lines earlier.
review_comments.author: danielhanchen

review_comments.body: The dataset route does authorize: launch_worker calls authorize_download(repo_id, repo_type, hf_token) for every account-scoped caller before spawn, so an unauthorized caller gets 404 with no worker, no completion and no grant. Reproduced the scenario at head: another account naming a cached private dataset without credentials ends with zero workers spawned, no grant and no visibility, and the denied claim leaves no active job.
review_comments.author: danielhanchen

review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Block hard links out of the read-only account root**

On macOS, a managed tool can use `link(2)`/`os.link` to place a regular-file hard link from the account-readable workspace into a writable root; the default sandbox is inside that same workspace and filesystem. The final rule denies only `SYMLINK` creation, so the writable-path rule still permits opening the hard link for mutation, which changes the original inode and lets tool code corrupt supposedly read-only databases, checkpoints, or other persistent account data. Deny hard-link creation across these roots as well as symbolic links.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
review_comments.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]

review_comments.body: Not reproducible. In SBPL file-link is a sibling of file-write*, not a child, so the profile's leading deny default already refuses link(2); the generated profile never allows file-link. On Linux the read-only account root is granted without LANDLOCK_ACCESS_FS_REFER, and a hard link out of it fails with EXDEV in a confined child on this host.
review_comments.author: danielhanchen

review_comments.body:
## CodeQL / Clear text storage of sensitive information

This stores sensitive data returned by [a call to loginWithPassword](1) as clear text.
This stores sensitive data returned by [a call to loginWithPassword](2) as clear text.

[Show more details](https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth/security/code-scanning/1297)
review_comments.author: github-advanced-security[bot]

review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Wait for chat generations before retiring account roots**

When the account has an active chat generation inside a provider or tool call, `cancel_all()` only sets its cancellation event and does not wait for the `ActiveGeneration` entry to drain. This function therefore continues to rename the account roots and can let DELETE return 204 while the deleted account still has API/tool/GPU work running; that entry also remains foreign work and can reject another account's model load. Apply the same drain-or-409 fence used below for image and video generation before retiring the roots.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
review_comments.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]

review_comments.body: Not changing this. Chat generations are signalled, not drained, by design: a generation parked in a provider or tool call has no bound, so a drain-or-409 fence here would make the account undeletable, unlike the bounded image and video slots below. The post-retirement window is already fenced by the tombstone: ensure_account_dir raises RetiredAccountError under root_retirement_lock, and both tool executors catch it, so a straggling generation cannot recreate or write the retired roots. Its active entry unwinds on exit or is reaped by the run sweep, and until then the arbiter refusing to evict a live stream is the intended answer. test_delete_retires_all_roots_and_recreated_username_inherits_nothing asserts this 204 with live entries.
review_comments.author: danielhanchen

review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Namespace Codex OAuth flows by account**

When two managed accounts independently use the same provider ID, this scoped existence check succeeds for either account, but the following `cancel_provider_flows(provider_id)` scans the process-global flow registry using only that ID. Deleting one account's provider therefore cancels the other account's pending browser listener or device poll; `start_flow()` has the same collision and cancels an existing pending flow when the second account starts authorization. Include the Studio account ID in transient flow ownership and all provider-wide cancellation/lookups.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
review_comments.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]

review_comments.body: Not changing this. Provider ids are minted server-side as uuid4 in create_provider_config and ProviderCreate has no id field, so two accounts cannot hold the same provider id; no provisioning path copies another account's rows either. Every Codex flow route also gates on a lookup in the acting account's own store, so an account cannot start or cancel a flow for an id it does not own. The fixture that reuses one literal id across accounts is a harness convenience, not a reachable state.
review_comments.author: danielhanchen

review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve committed residency across superseding loads**

Track the last successfully committed resident rather than the immediately preceding claimant. If Alice's model is resident, Bob starts an asynchronous load, and Carol supersedes it before Bob commits, this assignment records Bob as Carol's prior owner; Bob's superseded worker explicitly returns without rollback, so if Carol's load then fails, `restore_owner_account()` restores ownership to Bob even though Alice's model is still resident. Alice consequently sees her model as foreign while Bob can control or unload it, violating the account boundary.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
review_comments.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]

review_comments.body: Not changing this. The sequence cannot form: begin_load runs as the arbiter's register callback and refuses a second load while one is in flight, so Carol's claim is rejected before the prior owner is reassigned and _prior_account stays Alice. Every path that supersedes Bob's worker (unload, the arbiter evictor, an engine switch) unloads the resident pipeline first, and each restore_owner_account call site is gated on the previous pipeline still being resident, so the misattribution never runs. If Bob's load fails instead, his worker restores ownership to Alice before the error is published. Verified with the real arbiter and DiffusionBackend in both orderings.
review_comments.author: danielhanchen

review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scope index warm-up coordination by account**

The snapshot selected here is now account-specific, but `_warming`, `_warm_pending`, and the worker loop remain process-global. If Alice's warmer is running when Bob completes a download and calls `warm_index_soon()`, Bob's call returns without queueing Bob; `_warm_pending` merely makes Alice's account-bound worker scan Alice again. Bob's newly downloaded model can therefore remain absent from his resolver index until a later request happens to schedule another warm-up, causing intermittent model-not-found or wrong-resident responses under concurrent account activity.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pin recipe-provider connections to the validated public address**

For a managed account using an attacker-controlled hostname, DNS can return a public address during `public_provider_address()` and a loopback or LAN address when the Data Designer client later resolves the endpoint. Requiring HTTPS does not enforce public routing: TLS authenticates the hostname, and a private endpoint can present a valid certificate for that same attacker-controlled name; even a failed handshake still initiates a connection to the private service. Route these requests through the pinned public transport used for normal providers/MCP, or otherwise bind the actual connection to the address validated here.

review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restrict device access to the nodes tools actually require**

On a shared Linux host, managed tools run under the same Unix identity as Studio, so granting read, write, and ioctl access beneath all of `/dev` exposes same-UID resources outside the account workspace. For example, a tool can open another Studio/owner terminal through a guessed `/dev/pts/<n>` path, and it can access known same-UID objects under `/dev/shm`; root or privileged deployments additionally expose any mounted block and character devices. Grant only required pseudo-devices and explicitly selected accelerator nodes rather than the entire device tree (the macOS profile contains the analogous broad grant).

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

review_comments.body: Fixed in 434a4ee0c. The recipe job subprocess now installs a resolver guard for managed accounts: socket.getaddrinfo and gethostbyname refuse any answer that is not a global address, so a name that rebinds to loopback or the LAN after the endpoint check fails at resolve time and no connection is initiated. It is process-wide in the worker only, which is the process the engine dials from, and the HTTPS plus public-address check at recipe build time stays. Covered by test_managed_recipe_worker_refuses_names_that_resolve_privately.

review_comments.body: Fixed in 434a4ee0c. The Landlock rules no longer grant /dev; they grant the pseudo-devices (null, zero, full, random, urandom, tty) and the accelerator nodes that exist (nvidia*, nvidiactl, nvidia-uvm, nvidia-caps, dri, kfd). /dev is also treated as protected when the system roots are granted child by child, so the /run/shm link cannot reintroduce /dev/shm. The macOS profile now allows the same pseudo-devices by literal path instead of the /dev subpath. A runtime test confirms a managed tool reads /dev/urandom and writes /dev/null but cannot list /dev/shm.

### Motivation.


[The first-level directories of examples](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/main/examples) are offline_inference, online_serving and others. This Taxonomy system forces users to search through multiple folders to find examples for specific use cases. 

```

    def highlight(s, *args, **kwargs):

else:
    LEXER = PythonLexer()

class CLIContext:
    """Context Object for the CLI."""

    def __init__(self, app, no_color, workdir, quiet=False):
        """Initialize the CLI context."""
        self.app = app or get_current_app()
        self.no_color = no_color
        self.quiet = quiet
        self.workdir = workdir

class CeleryOption(click.Option):
    """Customized option for Celery."""

def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        """Initialize a Celery option."""
        self.help_group = kwargs.pop('help_group', None)
        self.default_value_from_context = kwargs.pop('default_value_from_context', None)
        super(CeleryOption, self).__init__(*args, **kwargs)

class CeleryCommand(click.Command):
    """Customized command for Celery."""

class CeleryDaemonCommand(CeleryCommand):
    """Daemon commands."""

def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        """Initialize a Celery command with common daemon options."""
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self.params.append(CeleryOption(('-f', '--logfile'), help_group="Daemonization Options"))
        self.params.append(CeleryOption(('--pidfile',), help_group="Daemonization Options"))
        self.params.append(CeleryOption(('--uid',), help_group="Daemonization Options"))
        self.params.append(CeleryOption(('--uid',), help_group="Daemonization Options"))
        self.params.append(CeleryOption(('--gid',), help_group="Daemonization Options"))
        self.params.append(CeleryOption(('--umask',), help_group="Daemonization Options"))
        self.params.append(CeleryOption(('--executable',), help_group="Daemonization Options"))

    """Comma separated list argument."""
name = "comma separated list"

def convert(self, value, param, ctx):

class Json(ParamType):

name = "json"
def convert(self, value, param, ctx):

name = "iso-86091"
def convert(self, value, param, ctx):

class ISO8601DateTimeOrFloat(ParamType):
    """ISO 8601 Date Time or float argument."""
name = "iso-86091 or float"

class LogLevel(click.Choice):
    """Log level option."""

JSON = Json()
ISO8601 = ISO8601DateTime()

COMMA_SEPARATED_LIST = CommaSeparatedList()

* Add auto expiry for DynamoDB backend (#5805)

* Add auto expiry for DynamoDB backend

This adds auto-expire support for the DynamoDB backend, via the DynamoDB
Time to Live feature.

* Require boto3>=1.9.178 for DynamoDB TTL support

boto3 version 1.9.178 requires botocore>=1.12.178.

botocore version 1.12.178 introduces support for the DynamoDB
UpdateTimeToLive call.

The UpdateTimeToLive call is used by the DynamoDB backend to enable TTL
support on a newly created table.

* Separate TTL handling from table creation

Handle TTL enabling/disabling separately from the table get-or-create
function.

Improve handling of cases where the TTL is already set to the desired
state.

DynamoDB only allows a single TTL update action within a fairly long
time window, so some problematic cases (changing the TTL attribute,
enabling/disabling TTL when it was recently modified) will raise
exceptions that have to be dealt with.

* Handle older boto3 versions

If the boto3 TTL methods are not found, log an informative error. If the
user wants to enable TTL, raise an exception; if TTL should be disabled,
simply return.

* Improve logging

- Handle exceptions by logging the error and re-raising

- Log (level debug) when the desired TTL state is already in place

* Add and use _has_ttl() convenience method

Additional changes:

- Handle exceptions when calling boto3's describe_time_to_live()

- Fix test cases for missing TTL methods

* Use gevent and eventlet wait() functions to remove busy-wait

Fixes issue #4999.

Calling AsyncResult.get() in a gevent context would cause the async Drainer to repeatedly call wait_for until the result was completed.  I've updated the code to have a specific implementation for gevent and eventlet that will cause wait_for to only return every "timeout" # of seconds, rather than repeatedly returning.

Some things I'd like some feedback on:
* Where's the best place to add test coverage for this?  It doesn't look like there are any tests that directly exercised the Drainer yet so I would probably look to add some of these to the backends/ unit tests.
* The way I did this for the Eventlet interface was to rely on the private _exit_event member of the GreenThread instance; to do this without relying on a private member would require some additional changes to the backend Drainer interface so that we could wait for an eventlet-specific event in wait_for().  I can do this, just wanted to get some feedback before.

* Add unit tests for Drainer classes

In order for this to work without monkeypatching in the tests, I needed to call sleep(0) to let the gevent/eventlet greenlets to yield control back to the calling thread.  I also made the check interval configurable in the drainer so that we didn't need to sleep multiples of 1 second in the tests.

* Fix eventlet auto-patching DNS resolver module on import

By default it looks like "import eventlet" imports the greendns module unless the environment EVENTLET_NO_GREENDNS is set to true.  This broke a pymongo test.

* Add tests ensuring that the greenlet loop isn't blocked

These tests make sure that while drain_events_until is running that other gevent/eventlet concurrency can run.

* Note about autodiscover_tasks and periodic tasks

This is particularly important for Django projects that put periodic tasks into each app's `tasks.py` and want to use one as a periodic task.  By the time `autodiscover_tasks()` loads those tasks, the `on_after_configure` Signal has already come and gone, so anything decorated with `@app.on_after_finalize.connect` will never be called.

If there's other documentation on this subject, I could not find it.

* Avoid race condition due to task duplication.

In some circumstances like a network partitioning, some tasks might
be duplicated. Sometimes, this lead to a race condition where a lost
task overwrites the result of the last successful task in the backend.

In order to avoid this race condition we prevent updating the result if
it's already in successful state.

This fix has been done for KV backends only and therefore won't work
with other backends.

* Add retry on recoverable exception for the backend

acks.late makes celery acknowledge messages only after processing and
storing result on the backend.

However, in case of backend unreachable, it will shadow a Retry
exception and put the task as failed in the backend not retrying the
task and acknoledging it on the broker.

With this new result_backend_always_retry setting, if the backend
exception is recoverable (to be defined per backend implementation),
it will retry the backend operation with an exponential backoff.

* Make elasticsearch backward compatible with 6.x

* Make ES retry storing updates in a better way

if existing value in the backend is success, then do nothing.
if it is a ready status, then update it only if new value is a ready status as well.
else update it.

This way, a SUCCESS cannot be overriden so that we do not loose
results but any ready state other than success (FAILURE, REVOKED) can
be overriden by another ready status (i.e. a SUCCESS)

* put back KeyValueStoreBackend.set method without state

It turns out it was breaking some other projects.
wrapping set method with _set_with_state, this way it will not break existing Backend.
while enabling this feature for other Backend.

Currently, only ElasticsearchBackend supports this feature.

It protects concurrent update to corrupt state in the backend.
Existing success cannot be overriden, nor a ready state by a non ready state.
i.e. a Retry state cannot override a Success or Failure.
As a result, chord_unlock task will not loop forever due to missing ready state on the backend.

issue_titles: Nested group-chain-group structure never succeeds
Remove Legacy Python (python2) support
Django celery fixup doesn't respect Django settings for PostgreSQL connections
Celery hangs indefinitely (instead of failing) if redis is not started
link_error tasks not run eagerly when using apply()
issue_bodies:
The structure like 

```
workflow = chain(
    t.task1.s(),
    chord(
        [
            t.task2.s(),
            chain(
                t.task3.s(),
                chord(
                    [t.task4.s(), t.task5.s()],
                    t.task6.s()
                )
            )
        ],
        t.task7.s()
    )
)
```

never succeeds. Task `t.task7` is never called, while other tasks succeed just fine. 

Replacing chords with groups did nothing. When I remove the inner chord, workflow finishes without any problems. Workflow also succeeds if I remove an inner chain.

The exact code that can be used to reproduce this issue as well as log messages are in [this gist](https://gist.github.com/traut/fcf5d76e07dd3ed6e54d)
Note that this will also remove `Jython` and `Pypy` support until they do not support python3.3+

When using the Django-Celery fixup to run background tasks for a Django web service, the tasks in the background do not respect the settings in Django for PostgreSQL (possibly other) connections.  Every task will always create a new connection no matter the Django settings.  Although it is possible to bypass this with the environment variable CELERY_DB_REUSE_MAX, it is preferred for it to follow the settings given in Django.

## Checklist

- [ ] I have included the output of ``celery -A proj report`` in the issue.
      (if you are not able to do this, then at least specify the Celery
       version affected).
Celery 4.0.2 with potentially all versions of Django (tested on 1.10.3 and 1.11.2)
- [X] I have verified that the issue exists against the `master` branch of Celery.

This line causes this "issue":
https://github.com/celery/celery/blob/master/celery/fixups/django.py#L186

## Steps to reproduce
Note that these steps require some monitoring service to be used, we have New Relic.
Note also that we use Heroku for this app in question.
1) Have a web facing process with Django that connects to your PostgreSQL database for ORM purposes
2) Have a worker process that also connects to the PostgreSQL for ORM purposes
3) Have the DATABASES['default']['CONN_MAX_AGE'] setting set to anything that isn't 0 (easiest to see with `None` for persistent connections)
4) Make multiple requests to the web portion of Django to cause some ORM activity (easiest to see if it happens on every request)
5) Get multiple tasks to execute on the worker that will cause some ORM activity (easiest to see if it happens on every task)
6) Use your monitoring service (New Relic in our case) to view a breakdown of all of the requests and worker activity.  In New Relic you can check this using the transaction tracing; select the endpoint/task that made the db queries and check the breakdown.

## Expected behavior
psycopg2:connect would occur rarely with an average calls per transaction <<< 1

## Actual behavior
psycopg2:connect occurs very rarely with an average calls per transaction of <<< 1 for the web processes.
psycopg2:connect occurs every time with an average calls per transaction of 1 for the worker processes.

## Potential Resolution
With my limited knowledge of Celery's inner workings, it feels like a fairly simple fix that I could make on a PR myself, but I wanted some input before I spend the time setting that all up.
This fix seems to work when monkey patched into the `DjangoWorkerFixup` class.
``` Python

def _close_database(self):
    try:
        # Use Django's built in method of closing old connections.
        # This ensures that the database settings are respected.
        self._db.close_old_connections()
    except AttributeError:
        # Legacy functionality if we can't use the old connections for whatever reason.
        for conn in self._db.connections.all():
            try:
                conn.close()
            except self.interface_errors:
                pass
            except self.DatabaseError as exc:

                try:
                    response = self.service.tabledata().insertAll(
                        projectId=self.project_id,
                        datasetId=dataset_id,
                        tableId=table_id,
                        body=body).execute()
                except HttpError as ex:
                    self.process_http_error(ex)

                # For streaming inserts, even if you receive a success HTTP
                # response code, you'll need to check the insertErrors property
                # of the response to determine if the row insertions were
                # successful, because it's possible that BigQuery was only
                # partially successful at inserting the rows.  See the `Success
                # HTTP Response Codes
                # <https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/
                #       streaming-data-into-bigquery#troubleshooting>`__
                # section

                insert_errors = response.get('insertErrors', None)
                if insert_errors:
                    self.process_insert_errors(insert_errors)

                sleep(1)  # Maintains the inserts "per second" rate per API
                rows = []

        self._print("\n")

issue_titles: [SIP-59] Proposal for Database migration standards
issue_bodies:
## [SIP] Proposal for database migration standards

### Motivation

Reduce pain around metadata database migrations by ensuring standards are followed and appropriate reviews are obtained before merging.

### Proposed Change

[SIP-57](https://github.com/apache/superset/issues/12566) (Semantic Versioning) introduced standards for avoiding breaking changes and general best practices for database migrations. The proposed changes below are in addition to those standards:

- All migrations must support rollbacks. Migrations must have a functional `downgrade` method to effectively rollback schema changes introduced in the `upgrade` method. If a migration makes changes to data that are not easily undone (e.g. #12960), the changes introduced must be non-breaking and idempotent.
- Migrations should be atomic and configured to complete fully in a single run, using a single transaction where appropriate. Any failures should trigger a rollback to the previous state. Partial migrations should be avoided.
- Any [constraints](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/13/core/constraints.html) added within a migration should include an explicit [name](https://alembic.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/naming.html), e.g. `sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(["user_id"], ["ab_user.id"], name='fk_user_id')`.
- PRs introducing database migrations must include runtime estimates and downtime expectations.
- Care should be taken to not introduce expensive DDL operations such as adding unnecessary constraints/indexes or setting column default values on tables potentially containing thousands of rows. [[1](https://www.craigkerstiens.com/2017/09/10/better-postgres-migrations/)][[2](https://severalnines.com/database-blog/schema-management-tips-mysql-mariadb)]
  - Indexes in Postgres tables should be added and removed [CONCURRENTLY](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/13/dialects/postgresql.html#indexes-with-concurrently).
- Migrations for breaking changes and cleanup (e.g. removal of columns) that should be held for the next major version, per the guidelines in [SIP-57](https://github.com/apache/superset/issues/12566), should be accumulated in `/superset/migrations/next/` for evaluation and inclusion in a future release.
- Establish Github [code owners](https://docs.github.com/en/github/creating-cloning-and-archiving-repositories/about-code-owners) on the `superset/migrations` directory to ensure PMC members are notified of new or updated migrations.
- Require **two** approvals for PRs that include database migrations, including committers from multiple organizations.
- PRs including database migrations should be kept open for a minimum review period of **two business days** to allow for adequate review, unless circumstances such as a critical vulnerability or breakage require faster turnaround.


### New or Changed Public Interfaces

None.

### New dependencies

No additional package dependencies.

### Migration Plan and Compatibility

Workflow changes only. PR template will be updated with guidelines. Process for running migrations unchanged.

### Rejected Alternatives

The status quo, which has resulted in quite a bit of thrash, deployment roadblocks and external discussions between Superset users.

context.pr_body:
Introduce `FlowDefinition`, a serializable model built from the Flow DSL's runtime metadata. It becomes the structural contract for Flow methods, triggers, routers, state, and configuration.

The visualization layer is the first consumer: `flow_structure` and `build_flow_structure` now project from the definition instead of re-introspecting the class. The runner still executes from live registries, but the definition gives future runners a single static contract to read.

This replaces AST source parsing for router return values, crew references, and state schema with runtime metadata plus explicit `@router(paths=...)` or `Literal`/`Enum` return hints. AST parsing was fragile and could silently fail for dynamic or non-inspectable methods.

The refactor removes obsolete introspection and serializer code:

* Delete `flow_serializer.py`, `flow/utils.py`, and `visualization/schema.py`
* Move flow structure modeling into `flow_definition.py`
* Simplify visualization building around the static definition contract

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Large refactor of flow structure, visualization, and router metadata with deleted public shims; runtime behavior should stay registry-based but static graphs may differ when router emits are not declared or inferrable.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a **serializable `FlowDefinition`** contract (methods, triggers, state, config, diagnostics, JSON/YAML export) and moves **Python class → definition** projection into **`dsl`** via `build_flow_definition`, with decorators recording **`FlowMethodDefinition`** fragments at decoration time.
> 
> **`Flow.flow_definition()`** is built lazily on first access; runtime still uses live registries but **`_router_paths`** becomes **`_router_emit`**. **`@router`** gains optional **`emit=`**, with **`Literal`/`Enum`** return hints when omitted, replacing AST parsing for static router outputs.
> 
> **Visualization** now projects from **`FlowDefinition`** only (no method source/signatures/OpenAPI); UI terminology shifts from **router paths** to **router events**. Removes **`flow_serializer`**, **`flow/utils`**, **`visualization/schema`**, and the public **`flow_structure`** export; **`human_feedback`** / **`persist`** align metadata (`__router_emit__`, `_human_feedback_llm`, persistence stamping) with the new contract.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit c9e171ded9cb88a5592f77c16cfe76163c6957c7. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

def test_threaded_docling_parse_table_matches_pypdfium(tmp_path: Path):
    """Both PDF backends must preserve the table from issue #3512."""
    pdf_path = tmp_path / "table_repro.pdf"
    rows = [
        ["Area of expertise", "Product Management", "Product Marketing"],
        ["Document Cloud", "Vamsi Vutukuru", "Nora Yau"],
        ["Acrobat", "Alex Chen", "Maria Lopez"],
        ["Sign", "Sam Patel", "Lena Frei"],
    ]

    figure = Figure(figsize=(8.27, 11.69))
    axis = figure.subplots()
    axis.axis("off")
    axis.text(
        0.5,
        0.95,
        "Contacts available for customer meetings",
        ha="center",
        fontsize=14,
    )
    table = axis.table(
        cellText=rows[1:],
        colLabels=rows[0],
        loc="center",
        cellLoc="center",
    )
    table.auto_set_font_size(False)
    table.set_fontsize(11)
    table.scale(1, 2.2)
    figure.savefig(pdf_path)

    documents = []
    backend_configs = [
        (PyPdfiumDocumentBackend, PdfBackendOptions()),
        (
            ThreadedDoclingParseDocumentBackend,
            ThreadedDoclingParseBackendOptions(parser_threads=1),
        ),
    ]
    for backend, backend_options in backend_configs:
        converter = DocumentConverter(
            format_options={
                InputFormat.PDF: PdfFormatOption(
                    pipeline_cls=StandardPdfPipeline,
                    backend=backend,
                    backend_options=backend_options,
                    pipeline_options=ThreadedPdfPipelineOptions(do_ocr=False),
                )
            }
        )
        result = converter.convert(pdf_path)

        assert result.status == ConversionStatus.SUCCESS
        documents.append(result.document)

    expected_cells = [cell for row in rows for cell in row]
    for document in documents:
        assert len(document.tables) == 1
        assert len(document.texts) == 1
        assert [
            cell.text.strip() for cell in document.tables[0].data.table_cells
        ] == expected_cells

    pypdfium_document, threaded_document = documents
    assert pypdfium_document.tables[0].data.num_rows == (
        threaded_document.tables[0].data.num_rows
    )
    assert pypdfium_document.tables[0].data.num_cols == (
        threaded_document.tables[0].data.num_cols
    )

context.pr_body:
This PR makes DoclingThreadedPdfParser the sole docling-parse implementation used by Docling and removes all PDFium usage from the docling-parse
  backend.

closes: #3512 

  ## Changes

  - Removed the legacy hybrid DoclingParsePageBackend implementation.
  - Replaced DoclingParseDocumentBackend with a deprecated compatibility wrapper around ThreadedDoclingParseDocumentBackend.
  - Removed all pypdfium2, managed PDFium backend, and pypdfium2_lock usage from docling_parse_backend.py.
  - Forwarded page ranges directly to DoclingThreadedPdfParser.load() using the API introduced in docling-parse 7.20.0.
  - Read document outlines from threaded parser annotations without opening a second parser.
  - Preserved outline destination page numbers and top-left coordinates.
  - Removed pypdfium2 from the format-pdf-docling extra.
  - Updated the minimum docling-parse version to 7.20.0.
  - Kept the standalone format-pdf-pypdfium2 backend and extra unchanged.

  ## Compatibility

  The following deprecated selections now emit a DeprecationWarning and resolve to ThreadedDoclingParseDocumentBackend:

  - DoclingParseDocumentBackend
  - DoclingParseV2DocumentBackend
  - DoclingParseV4DocumentBackend
  - PdfBackend.DOCLING_PARSE
  - PdfBackend.DLPARSE_V1
  - PdfBackend.DLPARSE_V2
  - PdfBackend.DLPARSE_V4

  The deprecated document backend no longer provides random page access. It follows the threaded backend contract and exposes pages through
  iter_pages().

  The CLI help now advertises only:

  - pypdfium2
  - threaded_docling_parse

  Deprecated backend values remain accepted for compatibility but are hidden from help.

  ## Motivation

  The threaded parser can now handle inclusive page ranges directly and expose document annotations, eliminating the remaining reasons for the docling-
  parse backend to depend on PDFium.

  This removes the PDFium lock from the default docling-parse path and avoids loading a second parser solely for outline extraction.
**Checklist:**

- [ ] Documentation has been updated, if necessary.
- [ ] Examples have been added, if necessary.
- [ ] Tests have been added, if necessary.
issue_titles: ThreadedDoclingParseDocumentBackend drops tables that DoclingParseDocumentBackend detects (same pipeline options, reproduced at parser_threads=1)
issue_bodies:
### Summary

Switching **only** the PDF backend from `DoclingParseDocumentBackend` to `ThreadedDoclingParseDocumentBackend` — with identical `ThreadedPdfPipelineOptions` and the same `StandardPdfPipeline` — causes a table to be missed. The serial backend extracts it as a `TableItem`; the threaded backend emits its content as loose text and produces **zero** tables.

The divergence is in the backend, not the table model (TableFormer is identical across both runs) and not concurrency (it persists at `parser_threads=1`).

### Environment

- `docling` 2.96.0
- `docling-core` 2.77.1
- `docling-parse` 6.2.0
- `docling-ibm-models` 3.13.2
- Python 3.14, macOS (Apple Silicon, arm64)

### Reproduction (fully self-contained — generates its own PDF)

```python
import warnings; warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# 1. Generate a minimal A4 PDF containing one simple table (matplotlib only).
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.27, 11.69))
ax.axis("off")
ax.text(0.5, 0.95, "Contacts available for customer meetings", ha="center", fontsize=14)
rows = [["Area of expertise", "Product Management", "Product Marketing"],
        ["Document Cloud", "Vamsi Vutukuru", "Nora Yau"],
        ["Acrobat", "Alex Chen", "Maria Lopez"],
        ["Sign", "Sam Patel", "Lena Frei"]]
tbl = ax.table(cellText=rows[1:], colLabels=rows[0], loc="center", cellLoc="center")
tbl.auto_set_font_size(False); tbl.set_fontsize(11); tbl.scale(1, 2.2)
fig.savefig("/tmp/table_repro.pdf"); plt.close(fig)

# 2. Convert with each backend — identical pipeline options, vary only the backend.
from docling.document_converter import DocumentConverter, PdfFormatOption
from docling.datamodel.base_models import InputFormat
from docling.backend.docling_parse_backend import (
    DoclingParseDocumentBackend, ThreadedDoclingParseDocumentBackend,
)
from docling.datamodel.backend_options import (
    ThreadedDoclingParseBackendOptions, PdfBackendOptions,
)
from docling.datamodel.pipeline_options import ThreadedPdfPipelineOptions

def run(label, backend, opts):
    fo = PdfFormatOption(pipeline_options=ThreadedPdfPipelineOptions(),
                         backend=backend, backend_options=opts)
    res = DocumentConverter(format_options={InputFormat.PDF: fo}).convert("/tmp/table_repro.pdf")
    print(f"{label}: tables={len(res.document.tables)} texts={len(res.document.texts)}")

run("serial  ", DoclingParseDocumentBackend, PdfBackendOptions())
run("threaded", ThreadedDoclingParseDocumentBackend, ThreadedDoclingParseBackendOptions())
run("threaded(parser_threads=1)", ThreadedDoclingParseDocumentBackend,
    ThreadedDoclingParseBackendOptions(parser_threads=1))
```

### Observed

```
serial  : tables=1 texts=1
threaded: tables=0 texts=2
threaded(parser_threads=1): tables=0
```

The serial backend detects the table; the threaded backend produces none, and the table's cell text is demoted into loose text items.

### Expected

Equal table extraction regardless of the PDF backend — `ThreadedDoclingParseDocumentBackend` at table-extraction parity with `DoclingParseDocumentBackend`.

### Notes

- **Not the table model.** TableFormer is identical in all three runs; only the backend differs.
- **Not concurrency.** The loss persists at `parser_threads=1` (fully serialised), so it is not a race / ordering bug.
- The threaded backend appears to feed different cell/layout data into the downstream table-structure stage, which then fails to cluster the table.
- Reproduced first on a real-world deck and then minimised to the self-contained PDF above.

context.pr_title: Refs #27308, #27753 -- Removed obsolete cookie test mixing bytes with str
context.pr_body:
Python 3 `SimpleCookie` treats all values as strings. Passing a bytes object coerces to the repr value.

From the [Python docs](https://docs.python.org/3/library/http.cookies.html#http.cookies.SimpleCookie):

> This class derives from BaseCookie and overrides value_decode() and value_encode() to be the identity and str() respectively.

Example:

```python
>>> from http.cookies import SimpleCookie
>>> c = SimpleCookie()
>>> c['test'] = b"\xf0"
>>> c
<SimpleCookie: test="b'\\xf0'">
```

Fixes warning of the form:

```
test_decode_2 (httpwrappers.tests.CookieTests) ... /usr/lib64/python3.6/http/cookies.py:634: BytesWarning: str() on a bytes instance
  strval = str(val)
```

Related to #2755 and #7346 .

`BaseEstimator.get_params` has logic which:
* sets a warnings filter to always show DeprecationWarnings. Always. Even if they're not from scikit-learn, or triggered outside of `get_params`.
* refuses to return from `get_params` a parameter (as defined by `BaseEstimator._get_param_names` to be a constructor parameter) whose attribute access raises a `DeprecationWarning`.

I find both these behaviours wrong. Clearly modifying the global warning filter setting is being a bad citizen (and doing so once per parameter is even weirder, even if duplicates are ignored by the warnings module), and we use a more circumspect formulation in `sklearn.__init__` which only affects warnings coming from `sklearn.*`.

While we rarely use `DeprecationWarnings` on parameter access (e.g. through a `property` with the deprecated parameter's name) within Scikit-learn itself, we *do* tend to allow parameters that are in the process of deprecation to have effect (e.g. `SGDClassifier.n_iter`), to be displayed by `get_params`, and to be set by `set_params`. (No doubt this `get_params` implementation was written before some of the "do not validate during construction" API policies were clear.) Whose code are we going to break if we just include the deprecated parameters in `get_params`??

I understand that `get_params` should not show any `DeprecationWarning`. And I understand that silencing them will in all cases run risks in terms of multithreading. (I also think we need to clarify the risks of solving #2755 with locking, as I think it really should be solved ASAP. But it's a separate issue.)

Ping @ogrisel.

context.pr_body:
Ticket [26682](https://code.djangoproject.com/ticket/26682). This PR contains few improvements on Oracle backend i.e.:
- autofield introspection,
- support for Oracle identity columns,
- support for use of Oracle sequences in bulk create.

review_comments.body:
If we use Oracle identity columns in tables in which we try to bulk insert then Oracle internally adds `sequence.nextval` to it. On the other hand we cannot use `sequence.nextval` in the following construct: _"A SELECT statement that is combined with another SELECT statement with the UNION, INTERSECT, or MINUS set operator"_ (see [documentation](http://docs.oracle.com/database/121/SQLRF/pseudocolumns002.htm#SQLRF00253)), hence I changed statement e.g.:
```sql
SELECT 'foo', 'foo', 'foo_sth' FROM dual
UNION ALL
SELECT 'bar', 'bar', 'bar_sth' FROM dual
```
to 
```sql
SELECT * FROM

issue_bodies:
## [SIP] Proposal for database migration standards

### Motivation

Reduce pain around metadata database migrations by ensuring standards are followed and appropriate reviews are obtained before merging.

### Proposed Change

[SIP-57](https://github.com/apache/superset/issues/12566) (Semantic Versioning) introduced standards for avoiding breaking changes and general best practices for database migrations. The proposed changes below are in addition to those standards:

- All migrations must support rollbacks. Migrations must have a functional `downgrade` method to effectively rollback schema changes introduced in the `upgrade` method. If a migration makes changes to data that are not easily undone (e.g. #12960), the changes introduced must be non-breaking and idempotent.
- Migrations should be atomic and configured to complete fully in a single run, using a single transaction where appropriate. Any failures should trigger a rollback to the previous state. Partial migrations should be avoided.
- Any [constraints](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/13/core/constraints.html) added within a migration should include an explicit [name](https://alembic.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/naming.html), e.g. `sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(["user_id"], ["ab_user.id"], name='fk_user_id')`.
- PRs introducing database migrations must include runtime estimates and downtime expectations.
- Care should be taken to not introduce expensive DDL operations such as adding unnecessary constraints/indexes or setting column default values on tables potentially containing thousands of rows. [[1](https://www.craigkerstiens.com/2017/09/10/better-postgres-migrations/)][[2](https://severalnines.com/database-blog/schema-management-tips-mysql-mariadb)]
  - Indexes in Postgres tables should be added and removed [CONCURRENTLY](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/13/dialects/postgresql.html#indexes-with-concurrently).
- Migrations for breaking changes and cleanup (e.g. removal of columns) that should be held for the next major version, per the guidelines in [SIP-57](https://github.com/apache/superset/issues/12566), should be accumulated in `/superset/migrations/next/` for evaluation and inclusion in a future release.
- Establish Github [code owners](https://docs.github.com/en/github/creating-cloning-and-archiving-repositories/about-code-owners) on the `superset/migrations` directory to ensure PMC members are notified of new or updated migrations.
- Require **two** approvals for PRs that include database migrations, including committers from multiple organizations.
- PRs including database migrations should be kept open for a minimum review period of **two business days** to allow for adequate review, unless circumstances such as a critical vulnerability or breakage require faster turnaround.


### New or Changed Public Interfaces

None.

### New dependencies

No additional package dependencies.

### Migration Plan and Compatibility

Workflow changes only. PR template will be updated with guidelines. Process for running migrations unchanged.

### Rejected Alternatives

The status quo, which has resulted in quite a bit of thrash, deployment roadblocks and external discussions between Superset users.

context.commit_message:
Sync sec-ch-ua with User-Agent and keep WebGL alive in stealth mode

Fix a bug where magic mode and per-request UA overrides would change
the User-Agent header without updating the sec-ch-ua (browser hint)
header to match. Anti-bot systems like Akamai detect this mismatch
as a bot signal.

Changes:
- Regenerate browser_hint via UAGen.generate_client_hints() whenever
  the UA is changed at crawl time (magic mode or explicit override)
- Re-apply updated headers to the page via set_extra_http_headers()
- Skip per-crawl UA override for persistent contexts where the UA is
  locked at launch time by Playwright's protocol layer
- Move --disable-gpu flags behind enable_stealth check so WebGL works
  via SwiftShader when stealth mode is active (missing WebGL is a
  detectable headless signal)
- Clean up old test scripts, add clean anti-bot test

issue_bodies:
In Pandas 2.0 NumericIndex should be the default numerical index and `Int64Index`, `UInt64Index` and `Float64Index` should be removed. See #41153 & #41272 for more discussion.

#41153 adds an internal attribute `_is_backward_compat_public_numeric_index` to the `Index` class (and its numeric child classes). This is only used to keep track of whether an index is a `NumericIndex` or one of its child indexes (`Int64Index`, `UInt64Index` and `Float64Index`) in order to maintain backwards compatability in Pandas 1.x. It will not be needed in pandas 2.0 after the child classes are removed and should removed in pandas 2.0 also.

This PR addresses the problem of low conversion throughput of `docx` documents introduced after the release `2.54.0`, in addition of other improvements:
- Simplify the parsing of tables with just text (no rich cells) and remove the addition and deletion of text items.
- Fix: cells holding a single run with formatting were considered for `TableCell` instead of `RichTableCell`
- Move nested function `group_cell_elements` out of `_handle_tables` for readability.
- Reuse method for finding inline pictures
- Add text item formatting for strike-through text
- Remove unnecessary argument `docx_obj` in functions
- Add test and test data for rich table cells
- Use fixtures to avoid converting same file multiple times
- Remove unnecessary imports
- Parse text formatted in superscript and subscript

Partially addressing #2509 

**Checklist:**

- [x] Examples have been added, if necessary.
- [x] Tests have been added, if necessary.

We found docling v2.55.0 and above becomes much slower on some of our docx and html documents.         with test_utils.device(should_use_gpu=True):

def _unique_padded(paths, size, pad):
    """Hash-based row-dedup, padded to a fixed leading size with `pad` rows.

    Mirrors `jax.numpy.unique(..., size=size, fill_value=pad, axis=0,
    return_inverse=True)` in observable behavior: the unique rows come
    first, followed by `(size - n_unique)` rows filled with `pad`, and
    `inverse` maps each input row to its index in the unique output.

    Internally avoids `torch.unique(dim=0)` (which sorts the full row
    tensor every call and dominates beam-search runtime) by hashing each
    path to int64 and deduplicating along that 1D axis. Collisions are
    detected by an explicit row-equality check on adjacent same-hash
    entries, so correctness does not rely on a collision-free hash.
    """
    n, t = paths.shape
    device = paths.device

    # Polynomial hash. Shift values to non-negative so all-`pad` rows
    # don't collapse to zero. Adjacent same-hash rows are verified for
    # equality below, so collisions stay correct.
    p = paths.to(torch.int64) + 1
    powers = _KNUTH_HASH_CONSTANT ** torch.arange(
        t, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
    )
    hashes = (p * powers).sum(dim=1)

    order = torch.argsort(hashes, stable=True)
    sorted_paths = paths[order]
    sorted_hashes = hashes[order]

    adj_hash_eq = sorted_hashes[1:] == sorted_hashes[:-1]
    adj_row_eq = (sorted_paths[1:] == sorted_paths[:-1]).all(dim=1)
    is_dup = adj_hash_eq & adj_row_eq
    is_first = torch.cat(
        [torch.ones(1, dtype=torch.bool, device=device), ~is_dup]
    )

    cum_first = torch.cumsum(is_first.to(torch.int64), dim=0) - 1
    inverse = torch.empty(n, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    inverse[order] = cum_first

    unique = sorted_paths[is_first]
    n_unique = unique.shape[0]
    if n_unique < size:
        pad_rows = torch.full(
            (size - n_unique, t),
            pad,
            dtype=unique.dtype,
            device=device,
        )
        unique = torch.cat([unique, pad_rows], dim=0)
    return unique, inverse

Closes #21978 
Closes #19506 
Closes https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/22835

High-level summary: SparseArray is an ExtensionArray. It's no longer an ndarray subclass. The actual data model hasn't changed at all, it's still an array and a `sparse_index`. Only now the sparse values are `self.sparse_values`, rather than `self`.

This isn't really close to being ready yet. I'm going to go through and self-review a bunch of things right now, will call out for others' opinions in specific places.


API discussions:

- [x] Why is the default kind inconsistent between SparseSeries and SparseArray?
    - Possibly get rid of block in a future PR
- [x] Should `.astype(np_dtype)` be sparse or dense?
    - sparse
- [x] What should the inferred type of an empty SparseArray be? `SparseArray([]).dtype`? NumPy defaults to float (`Sparse[float64]`), pandas typically uses object (`Sparse[object]`)
    - sparse
- [x] Policy for warning when converting to dense (e.g. https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/22325/files#diff-71caf9627e9687e837e4b1f86ecc6271R390). In the past, pandas would coerce to an ndarray all over the place. Now we at least have a *chance* of knowing when we're doing a bad thing, and warning about it.

review_comments.body:
For NumPy>=1.13, doing `ufunc(array)` first looks for `__array_ufunc__`. If that's defined on the class, it's called instead of the `__array__`, `__array_prepare__`, etc.

NumPy < 1.13 don't know about `__array_ufunc__` so they're never called when you do `ufunc(array)`. In other words, the only way you get into `__array_ufunc__` is if you're in numpy>=1.13, so it's safe to directly call the `__array_ufunc__` from within another `__array_ufunc__`.

def runTests(self, tests, parseAll=True, comment='#', fullDump=True, printResults=True, failureTests=False):
        """
        Execute the parse expression on a series of test strings, showing each
        test, the parsed results or where the parse failed. Quick and easy way to
        run a parse expression against a list of sample strings.
           
        Parameters:
         - tests - a list of separate test strings, or a multiline string of test strings
         - parseAll - (default=C{True}) - flag to pass to C{L{parseString}} when running tests           
         - comment - (default=C{'#'}) - expression for indicating embedded comments in the test 
              string; pass None to disable comment filtering
         - fullDump - (default=C{True}) - dump results as list followed by results names in nested outline;
              if False, only dump nested list
         - printResults - (default=C{True}) prints test output to stdout
         - failureTests - (default=C{False}) indicates if these tests are expected to fail parsing

        Returns: a (success, results) tuple, where success indicates that all tests succeeded
        (or failed if C{failureTests} is True), and the results contain a list of lines of each 
        test's output
        
        Example::
            number_expr = pyparsing_common.number.copy()

            result = number_expr.runTests('''
                # unsigned integer
                100
                # negative integer
                -100
                # float with scientific notation
                6.02e23
                # integer with scientific notation
                1e-12
                ''')
            print("Success" if result[0] else "Failed!")

            result = number_expr.runTests('''
                # stray character
                100Z
                # missing leading digit before '.'
                -.100
                # too many '.'
                3.14.159
                ''', failureTests=True)
            print("Success" if result[0] else "Failed!")
        prints::
            # unsigned integer
            100
            [100]

            # negative integer
            -100
            [-100]

            # float with scientific notation
            6.02e23
            [6.02e+23]

            # integer with scientific notation
            1e-12
            [1e-12]

            Success
            
            # stray character
            100Z
               ^
            FAIL: Expected end of text (at char 3), (line:1, col:4)

            # missing leading digit before '.'
            -.100
            ^
            FAIL: Expected {real number with scientific notation | real number | signed integer} (at char 0), (line:1, col:1)

            # too many '.'
            3.14.159
                ^
            FAIL: Expected end of text (at char 4), (line:1, col:5)

            Success

        Each test string must be on a single line. If you want to test a string that spans multiple
        lines, create a test like this::

            expr.runTest(r"this is a test\\n of strings that spans \\n 3 lines")
        
        (Note that this is a raw string literal, you must include the leading 'r'.)
        """
        if isinstance(tests, basestring):
            tests = list(map(str.strip, tests.rstrip().splitlines()))
        if isinstance(comment, basestring):
            comment = Literal(comment)
        allResults = []
        comments = []
        success = True
        for t in tests:
            if comment is not None and comment.matches(t, False) or comments and not t:
                comments.append(t)
                continue
            if not t:
                continue
            out = ['\n'.join(comments), t]
            comments = []
            try:
                t = t.replace(r'\n','\n')
                result = self.parseString(t, parseAll=parseAll)
                out.append(result.dump(full=fullDump))
                success = success and not failureTests
            except ParseBaseException as pe:
                fatal = "(FATAL)" if isinstance(pe, ParseFatalException) else ""
                if '\n' in t:
                    out.append(line(pe.loc, t))
                    out.append(' '*(col(pe.loc,t)-1) + '^' + fatal)
                else:
                    out.append(' '*pe.loc + '^' + fatal)
                out.append("FAIL: " + str(pe))
                success = success and failureTests
                result = pe
            except Exception as exc:
                out.append("FAIL-EXCEPTION: " + str(exc))
                success = success and failureTests
                result = exc

            if printResults:
                if fullDump:
                    out.append('')
                print('\n'.join(out))

            allResults.append((t, result))
        
        return success, allResults
