issue_titles: Nested group-chain-group structure never succeeds
Remove Legacy Python (python2) support
Django celery fixup doesn't respect Django settings for PostgreSQL connections
Celery hangs indefinitely (instead of failing) if redis is not started
link_error tasks not run eagerly when using apply()
issue_bodies:
The structure like 

```
workflow = chain(
    t.task1.s(),
    chord(
        [
            t.task2.s(),
            chain(
                t.task3.s(),
                chord(
                    [t.task4.s(), t.task5.s()],
                    t.task6.s()
                )
            )
        ],
        t.task7.s()
    )
)
```

never succeeds. Task `t.task7` is never called, while other tasks succeed just fine. 

Replacing chords with groups did nothing. When I remove the inner chord, workflow finishes without any problems. Workflow also succeeds if I remove an inner chain.

The exact code that can be used to reproduce this issue as well as log messages are in [this gist](https://gist.github.com/traut/fcf5d76e07dd3ed6e54d)
Note that this will also remove `Jython` and `Pypy` support until they do not support python3.3+

When using the Django-Celery fixup to run background tasks for a Django web service, the tasks in the background do not respect the settings in Django for PostgreSQL (possibly other) connections.  Every task will always create a new connection no matter the Django settings.  Although it is possible to bypass this with the environment variable CELERY_DB_REUSE_MAX, it is preferred for it to follow the settings given in Django.

## Checklist

- [ ] I have included the output of ``celery -A proj report`` in the issue.
      (if you are not able to do this, then at least specify the Celery
       version affected).
Celery 4.0.2 with potentially all versions of Django (tested on 1.10.3 and 1.11.2)
- [X] I have verified that the issue exists against the `master` branch of Celery.

This line causes this "issue":
https://github.com/celery/celery/blob/master/celery/fixups/django.py#L186

## Steps to reproduce
Note that these steps require some monitoring service to be used, we have New Relic.
Note also that we use Heroku for this app in question.
1) Have a web facing process with Django that connects to your PostgreSQL database for ORM purposes
2) Have a worker process that also connects to the PostgreSQL for ORM purposes
3) Have the DATABASES['default']['CONN_MAX_AGE'] setting set to anything that isn't 0 (easiest to see with `None` for persistent connections)
4) Make multiple requests to the web portion of Django to cause some ORM activity (easiest to see if it happens on every request)
5) Get multiple tasks to execute on the worker that will cause some ORM activity (easiest to see if it happens on every task)
6) Use your monitoring service (New Relic in our case) to view a breakdown of all of the requests and worker activity.  In New Relic you can check this using the transaction tracing; select the endpoint/task that made the db queries and check the breakdown.

## Expected behavior
psycopg2:connect would occur rarely with an average calls per transaction <<< 1

## Actual behavior
psycopg2:connect occurs very rarely with an average calls per transaction of <<< 1 for the web processes.
psycopg2:connect occurs every time with an average calls per transaction of 1 for the worker processes.

## Potential Resolution
With my limited knowledge of Celery's inner workings, it feels like a fairly simple fix that I could make on a PR myself, but I wanted some input before I spend the time setting that all up.
This fix seems to work when monkey patched into the `DjangoWorkerFixup` class.
``` Python

def _close_database(self):
    try:
        # Use Django's built in method of closing old connections.
        # This ensures that the database settings are respected.
        self._db.close_old_connections()
    except AttributeError:
        # Legacy functionality if we can't use the old connections for whatever reason.
        for conn in self._db.connections.all():
            try:
                conn.close()
            except self.interface_errors:
                pass
            except self.DatabaseError as exc:
                str_exc = str(exc)
                if 'closed' not in str_exc and 'not connected' not in str_exc:
                    raise

celery.fixups.django.DjangoWorkerFixup._close_database = _close_database
```

## Checklist

- [x] I have included the output of ``celery -A proj report`` in the issue.
      (if you are not able to do this, then at least specify the Celery
       version affected).
- [x] I have verified that the issue exists against the `master` branch of Celery.

```
software -> celery:4.1.0 (latentcall) kombu:4.1.0 py:2.7.12
            billiard:3.5.0.3 redis:2.10.6
platform -> system:Linux arch:64bit, ELF imp:CPython
loader   -> celery.loaders.app.AppLoader
settings -> transport:redis results:disabled

broker_url: u'redis://localhost:6379/0'
```

## Steps to reproduce

Stop `redis-server.`
Initialize a celery instance configured with redis.

## Expected behavior

I expected an `OperationalError` or another exception communicating that celery cannot connect to the broker server.

## Actual behavior

It hangs indefinitely.

## Why this is important

In the current situation is not possible to write automated functional and integration tests that check whether the software handles failures when brokers are not reachable.

## Checklist

- [x] I have included the output of ``celery -A proj report`` in the issue.
      (if you are not able to do this, then at least specify the Celery
       version affected).
- [x] I have verified that the issue exists against the `master` branch of Celery.

Tested using the included docker setup

```
$ celery -A tasks report
No handlers could be found for logger "vagrant"

software -> celery:4.2.0 (windowlicker) kombu:4.2.1 py:2.7.14
            billiard:3.5.0.4 py-amqp:2.3.2
platform -> system:Linux arch:64bit imp:CPython
loader   -> celery.loaders.app.AppLoader
settings -> transport:pyamqp results:redis://redis/

broker_url: u'amqp://guest:********@rabbit:5672//'
result_backend: u'redis://redis/'
```


## Steps to reproduce
Add `tasks.py`:

```python
# tasks.py

@app.task
def on_failure():
    print 'from on_failure'

@app.task
def error():
    raise ValueError('oh no!')
```
Run the tasks:
```python
>>> from tasks import error, on_failure
>>> error.apply(link_error=on_failure.si()).get()
```

## Expected behavior
Both `error` and `on_failure` to be executed eagerly.

## Actual behavior
`error` is executed eagerly and `on_failure` is executed on a worker.

	"""
	Format a template choice with responsive display based on terminal width.

	Styling:
	- Featured templates get [FEATURED] prefix
	- Author name included when width allows (except for default templates)
	- Everything turns orange when highlighted (InquirerPy's built-in behavior)

	Args:
		name: Template name
		metadata: Template metadata (description, featured, author)
		width: Terminal width in columns
		is_default: Whether this is a default template (default, advanced, tools)

	Returns:
		Formatted choice string
	"""
	is_featured = metadata.get('featured', False)
	description = metadata.get('description', '')
	author_name = metadata.get('author', {}).get('name', '') if isinstance(metadata.get('author'), dict) else ''

	# Build the choice string based on terminal width
	if width > 100:
		# Wide: show everything including author (except for default templates)
		if is_featured:
			if author_name:
				return f'[FEATURED] {name} by {author_name} - {description}'
			else:
				return f'[FEATURED] {name} - {description}'
		else:
			# Non-featured templates
			if author_name and not is_default:
				return f'{name} by {author_name} - {description}'
			else:
				return f'{name} - {description}'

	elif width > 60:
		# Medium: show name and description, no author
		if is_featured:
			return f'[FEATURED] {name} - {description}'
		else:
			return f'{name} - {description}'

	else:
		# Narrow: show name only
		return name

# Get terminal width for responsive formatting

		# Separate default and featured templates
		default_template_names = ['default', 'advanced', 'tools']
		featured_templates = [(name, info) for name, info in INIT_TEMPLATES.items() if info.get('featured', False)]
		other_templates = [(name, info) for name, info in INIT_TEMPLATES.items() if name not in default_template_names and not info.get('featured', False)]

		# Sort by last_modified_date (most recent first)
		def get_last_modified(item):
			name, info = item
			date_str = info.get('author', {}).get('last_modified_date', '1970-01-01') if isinstance(info.get('author'), dict) else '1970-01-01'
			return date_str

		# Sort default templates by last modified
		default_templates = [(name, INIT_TEMPLATES[name]) for name in default_template_names if name in INIT_TEMPLATES]
		default_templates.sort(key=get_last_modified, reverse=True)

		# Sort featured and other templates by last modified
		featured_templates.sort(key=get_last_modified, reverse=True)
		other_templates.sort(key=get_last_modified, reverse=True)

		# Build choices in order: defaults first, then featured, then others
		choices = []

		# Add default templates
		for i, (name, info) in enumerate(default_templates):
			formatted = _format_choice(name, info, width, is_default=True)

		for name, info in other_templates:

			choices.append(Choice(name=formatted, value=name))

Dont perform implicit close/warning on `__del__` (#2026)

* Version 0.21.3

* Don't perform implict close on __del__
context.pr_body:
- Prompted by discussion #1951
- Closes #2024

We currently attempt to perform a bit of hand-holding for cases where a client instance has not been closed at the point it is deleted. The reasoning here was to try to give users a bit more of a guard against unintentional resource leaks.

Our behaviour here was...

* For sync clients, automatically `.close()` clients on `__del__`, if they're still open.
* For async clients, issue a warning on `__del__`, if they're still open.

As it turns out, this *just isn't reliable*. We really can't do this properly, because if `__del__` is called at `atexit` then there's all sorted of bit of stdlib that may not be available. We can't reliably call into `warnings.warn`, and it turns out we can't even reliably access the properties on an `intenum` class. Geez.

So. Let's just *not do this anymore*.

If you're leaking client instances (which as it happens, zillions of `requests` and `urllib3` using codebases currently already do.) Then okay, that's just the way it is. I'm not sure what flags you'd need to enable in python to have the system warn you about when that's the case, but we should rely on that level of warning, rather than attempting to add any ourselves.

Better that we stick with the current status-quo, than attempt to do better and actually just end up with user-hostile exceptions or undefined behaviours.

Once we have a sync interface on the `Response` we can have a more graceful implementation here, too, along these lines...

```python
if stream is None:

    self.stream = ByteStream(content)
    self.read()
else:
    # This is the standard case. Dispatchers pass a `stream=<Stream>` argument to the response.
    self.stream = stream
```

## Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist
- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.


## Purpose

Follow-up to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/21227

**`--task` (`model_config.task`) is now deprecated.** Users are expected to pass `--runner` and/or `--convert` instead, according to the logic of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/21470/files#diff-7eaad0b7dee0626bf29d10081b0f0c5e3ea15a4af97e7b182a4e0d35f8346953R610-R670

This PR also makes it a lot easier to add new converters without having to wrestle with model registry, since `registry.is_pooling_model` is now based on the un-converted architecture.

FIX https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/21514

cc @maxdebayser @noooop @22quinn 

## Test Plan

Added new tests to check the handling of passing custom `--pooling`.

The existing tests, especially those that are updated in this PR, should pass.

Updated all documentation to stop referring to `--task`.

def _install_fakes(monkeypatch, captured_params: list[dict[str, object]]) -> list[str]:
    """Fake only inference + downloading; keep rapidocr's real model registry.

    Returns the list that will collect every downloaded URL.
    """
    import rapidocr

monkeypatch.setattr(rapidocr, "RapidOCR", FakeRapidOCR)

    downloaded_urls: list[str] = []

    def fake_download_url_with_progress(url: str, *, progress: bool) -> BytesIO:
        del progress
        downloaded_urls.append(url)
        return BytesIO(b"dummy content")

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "docling.models.stages.ocr.rapid_ocr_model.download_url_with_progress",
        fake_download_url_with_progress,
return downloaded_urls

def _seed(artifacts_path: Path, backend: str, lang: str) -> None:
    """Prefetch one `(backend, lang)` set into artifacts_path, the way a user would."""
    RapidOcrModel.download_models(
        backend=backend,
        lang=lang,
        local_dir=artifacts_path / RapidOcrModel._model_repo_folder,
    )

def _build(
    monkeypatch,
    options: RapidOcrOptions,
    artifacts_path: Path | None,
    *,
    seed: tuple[str, str] | None = None,
):
    captured_params: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    downloaded = _install_fakes(monkeypatch, captured_params)
    if seed is not None:
        assert artifacts_path is not None
        _seed(artifacts_path, *seed)
        # Prefetching is the setup step; only what the model itself fetches is under test.
        downloaded.clear()

artifacts_path=artifacts_path,
        options=options,

return captured_params[0], downloaded


# --- resolution -------------------------------------------------------------


def _resolved(lang: str, backend: str):
    """The (version, registry token) pair the assertions below care about."""
    spec = _resolve_rapidocr(lang, backend)
    return spec.ppocr_version, spec.rapidocr_lang_token


def test_resolve_populates_the_whole_spec() -> None:
    from rapidocr.utils.typings import OCRVersion

    spec = _resolve_rapidocr("zh", "onnxruntime")
    assert spec.backend == "onnxruntime"
    # The user's token is preserved verbatim, the registry token is normalized.
    assert spec.user_lang == "zh"
    assert spec.rapidocr_lang_token == "ch"
    assert spec.ppocr_version == OCRVersion.PPOCRV6


def test_resolve_defaults_to_ppocrv6_chinese() -> None:
    from rapidocr.utils.typings import OCRVersion

    assert _resolved("chinese", "onnxruntime") == (OCRVersion.PPOCRV6, "ch")
    assert _resolved("zh", "onnxruntime") == (OCRVersion.PPOCRV6, "ch")


def test_resolve_english_and_latin_use_ppocrv6() -> None:
    from rapidocr.utils.typings import OCRVersion

    assert _resolved("english", "onnxruntime") == (OCRVersion.PPOCRV6, "en")
    assert _resolved("en", "torch") == (OCRVersion.PPOCRV6, "en")
    assert _resolved("de", "onnxruntime") == (OCRVersion.PPOCRV6, "de")
    assert _resolved("fr", "onnxruntime") == (OCRVersion.PPOCRV6, "fr")


def test_resolve_script_families_route_by_backend() -> None:
    from rapidocr.utils.typings import OCRVersion

    # onnxruntime/openvino/paddle -> PP-OCRv5
    assert _resolved("th", "onnxruntime") == (OCRVersion.PPOCRV5, "th")
    assert _resolved("cyrillic", "onnxruntime") == (OCRVersion.PPOCRV5, "cyrillic")
    # torch -> PP-OCRv4
    assert _resolved("arabic", "torch") == (OCRVersion.PPOCRV4, "arabic")


def test_resolve_raises_on_unsupported_language() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        _resolve_rapidocr("klingon", "onnxruntime")
    # Thai is a PP-OCRv5 language, not served by the torch PP-OCRv4 backbone.
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        _resolve_rapidocr("th", "torch")

def test_rapidocr_default_onnx_uses_ppocrv6(monkeypatch, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    params, downloaded = _build(
        monkeypatch,

context.pr_body:
Reworks how `RapidOcrModel` maps a user's requested language and backend onto concrete PP-OCR checkpoints, so Docling can serve every language RapidOCR supports instead of just `chinese`/`english`.

Previously the model shipped hand-maintained per-language, per-backend model-path tables that were hard to extend and effectively capped support at a couple of languages. This PR replaces them with a resolver that picks the right PP-OCR version and recognizer for a given `(lang, backend)` pair and fetches assets on demand.

**Resolution procedure:**

1. Get the user's input for the language and the rapidocr backend (or the default values).
2. Use `RapidOCR/python/rapidocr/utils/model_resolver.py` to check if the language is supported in PPOCRv6:
   a. First pass the input language through the `COMMON_LANG_ALIASES.get(input_lang, input_lang)`
   b. Check if the output of a exists in `PP_OCRV6_LANGS`
   - If yes download the PPOCR-v6 checkpoints. Return.
3. Else if the backend is torch:
   a. If the input language is in: `arabic, cyrillic, devanagari, ka, korean, latin, ta, te`
   download the PPOCR-v4 checkpoints. Return.
   b. Else raise exception that the asked language is not supported by that backbone
4. Else:
   a. If the language input is any of: `arabic, ch, cyrillic, devanagari, el, en, eslav, korean, latin, ta, te, th`
      download the PPOCR-v5 checkpoints. Return.
   b. Else raise exception that the asked language is not supported by that backbone


**RapidOCR model artifacts download:**

1. Extend the `docling-tools` CLI to introduce the repeated parameter `--rapidocr-backend-lang`:
   - This allows to download the RapidOCR artifacts for a combination of `backend:language`
   - The actual URL is still provided by `RapidOCR.InferSession`.
   - Docling's code decides the saving path and filename.
   - E.g. if we want to download greek for the `onnxruntime` backend and `korean` for torch backend:

```
docling-tools models download rapidocr \
    --rapidocr-backend-lang onnxruntime:el \
    --rapidocr-backend-lang torch:korean \
    --output-dir "${MODELS_SAVE_DIR}"
``` 

2. If the user has NOT provided `artifacts_path` the downloading is fully delegated to RapidOCR lib:
   - This allows to use the artifacts bundled in the python package.
3. If `artifacts_path` has been provided, RapidOCR runs in an "air-gapped" environment:
   - No artifacts downloads.
   - If the required artifacts are not present in `artifacts_path` the user receives an exception with an informative message about which backend/language should be pre-fetched and the particular files that should be placed in `artifacts_path`.


In case the user has provided custom paths for each individual model (det/rec/cls), they are used instead.

context.pr_body:
## Summary

- Replace the 2-LLM-call add pipeline with single-pass additive extraction using `ADDITIVE_EXTRACTION_PROMPT` (ADD-only, memories accumulate with `linked_memory_ids`)
- Add hybrid search combining semantic + BM25 keyword matching + entity boost with additive scoring: `(semantic + bm25 + entity_boost) / max_possible`
- Add native `keyword_search()` to 15 vector store adapters (Qdrant, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Azure AI Search, Weaviate, Redis, PGVector, Pinecone, Databricks, MongoDB, Milvus, Baidu, Upstash, Azure MySQL, Vertex AI)
- Add spaCy-based entity extraction and linking via second vector collection (`{collection}_entities`)
- Add batch embedding, batch persist, batch entity linking (8-phase pipeline) for both sync `Memory` and async `AsyncMemory` at full parity
- Add `embed_batch()` to embedding base class with native OpenAI/Azure overrides
- Add message persistence in SQLite (rolling window of 10 per session scope) for LLM context
- spaCy is an optional dependency (`pip install mem0ai[nlp]`) — system degrades gracefully without it

## Breaking Changes

| Change | Migration |
|--------|-----------|
| `add()` only returns `"ADD"` events (no `"UPDATE"`/`"DELETE"`) | Memories accumulate; accept ADD-only results |
| `search()` default `threshold` changed to `0.1` (was `None`) | Pass `threshold=0.0` for old behavior |
| `search()` `score` is now combined additive score (was raw cosine) | Use `score_breakdown.semantic` for old value |
| `search()` default `rerank` changed to `False` (was `True`) | Pass `rerank=True` for old behavior |
| `qdrant-client>=1.12.0` required (was `>=1.9.1`) | Upgrade qdrant-client |

## Test Coverage

- [x] Added unit tests for lemmatization, entity extraction, scoring (39 tests passing)
- [x] Updated test_main.py for v3 pipeline expectations
- [ ] Integration tests with real vector stores (manual testing needed)
- [x] Tested graceful degradation without spaCy installed

def _assert_no_error(error, exception_class=None):
    """
    Checks the return code and throws an exception if there is an error to
    report
    """
    if error == 0:
        return

    cf_error_string = Security.SecCopyErrorMessageString(error, None)
    output = _cf_string_to_unicode(cf_error_string)
    CoreFoundation.CFRelease(cf_error_string)

    if output is None or output == u'':
        output = u'OSStatus %s' % error

    if exception_class is None:
        exception_class = ssl.SSLError

    raise exception_class(output)

context.pr_body:
Implements [SLEP010](https://scikit-learn-enhancement-proposals.readthedocs.io/en/latest/slep010/proposal.html)

Superseds #13603 

The `_validate_data` method is only called in `fit` and `partial_fit`. I will open other PRs later for `predict`, `transform`, etc.

Please note that while the SLEP was under review, https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/pull/15557 was merged which allows the Gaussian Processes to support sequences of variable length. That use-case isn't covered by the SLEP. For now, the `n_features_in_` doesn't exist if a GP is passed a non-2d array.

# ───────────────── safe config‑dump helper ─────────────────
ALLOWED_TYPES = {
    "CrawlerRunConfig": CrawlerRunConfig,
    "BrowserConfig": BrowserConfig,
}

def _safe_eval_config(expr: str) -> dict:
    """
    Accept exactly one top‑level call to CrawlerRunConfig(...) or BrowserConfig(...).
    Whatever is inside the parentheses is fine *except* further function calls
    (so no  __import__('os') stuff).  All public names from crawl4ai are available
    when we eval.
    """
    tree = ast.parse(expr, mode="eval")

    # must be a single call
    if not isinstance(tree.body, ast.Call):
        raise ValueError("Expression must be a single constructor call")

    call = tree.body
    if not (isinstance(call.func, ast.Name) and call.func.id in {"CrawlerRunConfig", "BrowserConfig"}):
        raise ValueError("Only CrawlerRunConfig(...) or BrowserConfig(...) are allowed")

    # forbid nested calls to keep the surface tiny
    for node in ast.walk(call):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Call) and node is not call:
            raise ValueError("Nested function calls are not permitted")

    # expose everything that crawl4ai exports, nothing else
    safe_env = {name: getattr(_c4, name) for name in dir(_c4) if not name.startswith("_")}

# Summary

Replaces the four separate memory types (`ShortTermMemory`, `LongTermMemory`, `EntityMemory`, `ExternalMemory`) with a single `Memory` class where both encoding and retrieval are LLM-driven. Results are ranked by a composite score blending semantic similarity, recency, and importance -- not just vector distance.

# Key changes

### **Unified `Memory` class.** 
One API: `remember()`, `recall()`, `forget()`. On save, the LLM infers scope, categories, and importance. On recall, a multi-step `RecallFlow` assesses query complexity, monitors its own confidence, and deepens search when uncertain. A `ConsolidationFlow` on save detects near-duplicate records and merges/updates/deletes them automatically.

### **Composite scoring.** 
`semantic_weight * similarity + recency_weight * decay + importance_weight * importance`. Applied in both shallow and deep recall paths, including the confidence router that decides "synthesize vs explore deeper."

### **Hierarchical scopes.**
Memories organize into a tree (`/company/engineering`, `/project/alpha`). `MemoryScope` restricts operations to a subtree; `MemorySlice` combines multiple scopes into one view.

### **Config lives on `Memory`.**
All tunable knobs are kwargs: `Memory(recency_weight=0.5, exploration_budget=2)`. No separate config object needed.

### **Simplified `Crew.memory`.** 
Single field replaces `memory` + `memory_instance`. `Crew(memory=True)` creates defaults; `Crew(memory=Memory(...))` for custom config.

##$ **Memory TUI.** 
`crewai memory` opens a terminal UI for browsing scopes, viewing entries with pagination, and running recall queries. `textual` is now a core dependency.

##$ **Flow proxy fix.**
`LockedListProxy` and `LockedDictProxy` now subclass `list`/`dict` so `isinstance` checks pass in LanceDB, Pydantic, etc.

# How memory integrates across the stack

### **Crew.** 
`Crew(memory=True)` creates a default `Memory()`. Pass `Crew(memory=Memory(...))` for custom tuning. All agents in the crew share it. After each task, the executor calls `extract_memories()` to decompose the raw result into atomic facts, then `remember()` on each -- so the crew's knowledge base grows automatically as tasks complete.

### **Agent.** 
- During task execution, the agent recalls relevant memories and injects them into the task context. The agent uses the crew's shared memory unless it has its own `memory` field set, in which case it uses that (can be a `Memory`, `MemoryScope`, or `MemorySlice`).

### **LiteAgent.** 
Same pattern: `LiteAgent(memory=True)` or `LiteAgent(memory=Memory(...))`. Before each turn, it recalls memories matching the user's latest message and appends them to the system prompt. After each turn, it extracts and remembers facts from the response.

### **Flow.** 
Every Flow automatically gets a `Memory` instance. Flow methods can call `self.remember()`, `self.recall()`, and `self.extract_memories()` directly -- memory is a first-class capability, not something wired up externally.

# What was removed

`ShortTermMemory`, `LongTermMemory`, `EntityMemory`, `ExternalMemory`, `ContextualMemory`, and their storage backends (`rag_storage.py`, `ltm_sqlite_storage.py`, `mem0_storage.py`). All replaced by unified `Memory` + `LanceDBStorage`.

## `__eq__` not overridden when adding attributes The class 'LockedListProxy' does not override '__eq__', but adds the new attribute _list.
The class 'LockedListProxy' does not override '__eq__', but adds the new attribute _lock. --- In general, when a subclass of a built-in container stores its actual data in a separate attribute instead of the base class' storage, it must override __eq__ to compare based on that actual data; otherwise the base class' equality ignores the extra attribute and gives wrong results. The best fix here is to implement __eq__ (and __ne__ for consistency) on LockedListProxy so that it compares self._list to the other object, mirroring list's semantics. This preserves existing functionality (thread-safe mutations, list-like behavior, isinstance(proxy, list) checks) while fixing equality.

Concretely, in lib/crewai/src/crewai/flow/flow.py, inside class LockedListProxy, add:

  • A __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool method that:
    • If other is another LockedListProxy, compares their underlying _list attributes.
    • Otherwise, compares self._list directly to other, so LockedListProxy([...]) == [...] behaves like a normal list.
  • A __ne__(self, other: object) -> bool method that returns the logical negation of __eq__, ensuring Python 3 code that still relies on != gets consistent behavior.

No new imports are needed; this is pure Python behavior within the existing class. Place these methods near the other dunder methods (__repr__, __bool__) to keep the class organized. No other files or regions need modification.

The class 'LockedDictProxy' does not override '__eq__', but adds the new attribute _lock. --- In general, when a subclass of a built-in like dict or list does not use the base class’s internal storage (e.g., by not calling super().__init__() and instead storing data in a separate attribute), you should override __eq__ (and usually __ne__) so that equality is defined in terms of the actual underlying data structure, not the empty base-class container. This keeps equality semantics consistent with the built-in type the class is mimicking.

For LockedDictProxy, the best fix is to implement __eq__ (and __ne__ delegating to __eq__) so that:

  • Comparing a LockedDictProxy to any Mapping (like a plain dict) uses the wrapped _dict compared to the other mapping.
  • For unsupported types, returning NotImplemented lets Python fall back to the other operand’s __eq__.

This preserves existing external behavior (it still looks like a dict, uses the same underlying _dict object, and remains thread-safe) while fixing equality. The new methods should be added inside LockedDictProxy in lib/crewai/src/crewai/flow/flow.py, near the other core dunder methods (e.g., after __delitem__ or after the existing proxy methods), and they can use threading.Lock that is already stored in self._lock. @pytest.mark.usefixtures("mock_camera")
async def test_camera_proxy_query_token_auth(
    hass: HomeAssistant, hass_client_no_auth: ClientSessionGenerator
) -> None:
    """Test the camera proxy authenticates via the access token query param."""
    client = await hass_client_no_auth()

    state = hass.states.get("camera.demo_camera")
    assert state is not None

    # A valid access token in the query param authenticates the request
    resp = await client.get(state.attributes["entity_picture"])
    assert resp.status == HTTPStatus.OK
    assert await resp.read() == b"Test"

    # Without a token the request is unauthorized
    resp = await client.get("/api/camera_proxy/camera.demo_camera")
    assert resp.status == HTTPStatus.UNAUTHORIZED

    # An invalid token is also unauthorized
    resp = await client.get("/api/camera_proxy/camera.demo_camera?token=invalid")
    assert resp.status == HTTPStatus.UNAUTHORIZED

def inverse_sigmoid(x, eps=1e-5):
    x = x.clamp(min=0, max=1)
    x1 = x.clamp(min=eps)
    x2 = (1 - x).clamp(min=eps)
    return torch.log(x1 / x2)


class RTDetrV2Decoder(RTDetrV2PreTrainedModel):
    def __init__(self, config: RTDetrV2Config):
        super().__init__(config)

        self.dropout = config.dropout
        self.layers = nn.ModuleList([RTDetrV2DecoderLayer(config) for _ in range(config.decoder_layers)])
        self.query_pos_head = RTDetrV2MLPPredictionHead(config, 4, 2 * config.d_model, config.d_model, num_layers=2)

        # hack implementation for iterative bounding box refinement and two-stage Deformable DETR
        self.bbox_embed = None
        self.class_embed = None

        # Initialize weights and apply final processing
        self.post_init()

    def forward(
        self,
        inputs_embeds=None,
        encoder_hidden_states=None,
        encoder_attention_mask=None,
        position_embeddings=None,
        reference_points=None,
        spatial_shapes=None,
        spatial_shapes_list=None,
        level_start_index=None,
        valid_ratios=None,
        output_attentions=None,
        output_hidden_states=None,
        return_dict=None,
    ):
        r"""
        Args:
            inputs_embeds (`torch.FloatTensor` of shape `(batch_size, num_queries, hidden_size)`):
                The query embeddings that are passed into the decoder.
            encoder_hidden_states (`torch.FloatTensor` of shape `(batch_size, sequence_length, hidden_size)`, *optional*):
                Sequence of hidden-states at the output of the last layer of the encoder. Used in the cross-attention
                of the decoder.
            encoder_attention_mask (`torch.LongTensor` of shape `(batch_size, sequence_length)`, *optional*):
                Mask to avoid performing cross-attention on padding pixel_values of the encoder. Mask values selected
                in `[0, 1]`:
                - 1 for pixels that are real (i.e. **not masked**),
                - 0 for pixels that are padding (i.e. **masked**).
            position_embeddings (`torch.FloatTensor` of shape `(batch_size, num_queries, hidden_size)`, *optional*):
                Position embeddings that are added to the queries and keys in each self-attention layer.
            reference_points (`torch.FloatTensor` of shape `(batch_size, num_queries, 4)` is `as_two_stage` else `(batch_size, num_queries, 2)` or , *optional*):
                Reference point in range `[0, 1]`, top-left (0,0), bottom-right (1, 1), including padding area.
            spatial_shapes (`torch.FloatTensor` of shape `(num_feature_levels, 2)`):
                Spatial shapes of the feature maps.
            level_start_index (`torch.LongTensor` of shape `(num_feature_levels)`, *optional*):
                Indexes for the start of each feature level. In range `[0, sequence_length]`.
            valid_ratios (`torch.FloatTensor` of shape `(batch_size, num_feature_levels, 2)`, *optional*):
                Ratio of valid area in each feature level.

            output_attentions (`bool`, *optional*):
                Whether or not to return the attentions tensors of all attention layers. See `attentions` under
                returned tensors for more detail.
            output_hidden_states (`bool`, *optional*):
                Whether or not to return the hidden states of all layers. See `hidden_states` under returned tensors
                for more detail.
            return_dict (`bool`, *optional*):
                Whether or not to return a [`~file_utils.ModelOutput`] instead of a plain tuple.
        """
        output_attentions = output_attentions if output_attentions is not None else self.config.output_attentions
        output_hidden_states = (
            output_hidden_states if output_hidden_states is not None else self.config.output_hidden_states
        )
        return_dict = return_dict if return_dict is not None else self.config.use_return_dict

        if inputs_embeds is not None:
            hidden_states = inputs_embeds

        # decoder layers
        all_hidden_states = () if output_hidden_states else None
        all_self_attns = () if output_attentions else None
        all_cross_attentions = () if (output_attentions and encoder_hidden_states is not None) else None
        intermediate = ()
        intermediate_reference_points = ()
        intermediate_logits = ()

        reference_points = F.sigmoid(reference_points)

        # https://github.com/lyuwenyu/RT-DETR/blob/94f5e16708329d2f2716426868ec89aa774af016/RTDetrV2_pytorch/src/zoo/RTDetrV2/RTDetrV2_decoder.py#L252
        for idx, decoder_layer in enumerate(self.layers):
            reference_points_input = reference_points.unsqueeze(2)
            position_embeddings = self.query_pos_head(reference_points)

            if output_hidden_states:
                all_hidden_states += (hidden_states,)

            layer_outputs = decoder_layer(
                hidden_states,
                position_embeddings=position_embeddings,
                encoder_hidden_states=encoder_hidden_states,
                reference_points=reference_points_input,
                spatial_shapes=spatial_shapes,
                spatial_shapes_list=spatial_shapes_list,
                level_start_index=level_start_index,
                encoder_attention_mask=encoder_attention_mask,
                output_attentions=output_attentions,
            )

            hidden_states = layer_outputs[0]

            # hack implementation for iterative bounding box refinement
            if self.bbox_embed is not None:
                predicted_corners = self.bbox_embed[idx](hidden_states)
                new_reference_points = F.sigmoid(predicted_corners + inverse_sigmoid(reference_points))
                reference_points = new_reference_points.detach()

            intermediate += (hidden_states,)
            intermediate_reference_points += (
                (new_reference_points,) if self.bbox_embed is not None else (reference_points,)
            )

            if self.class_embed is not None:
                logits = self.class_embed[idx](hidden_states)
                intermediate_logits += (logits,)

            if output_attentions:
                all_self_attns += (layer_outputs[1],)

                if encoder_hidden_states is not None:
                    all_cross_attentions += (layer_outputs[2],)

        # Keep batch_size as first dimension
        intermediate = torch.stack(intermediate, dim=1)
        intermediate_reference_points = torch.stack(intermediate_reference_points, dim=1)
        if self.class_embed is not None:
            intermediate_logits = torch.stack(intermediate_logits, dim=1)

        # add hidden states from the last decoder layer
        if output_hidden_states:
            all_hidden_states += (hidden_states,)

        if not return_dict:
            return tuple(
                v
                for v in [
                    hidden_states,
                    intermediate,
                    intermediate_logits,
                    intermediate_reference_points,
                    all_hidden_states,
                    all_self_attns,
                    all_cross_attentions,
                ]
                if v is not None
            )
        return RTDetrV2DecoderOutput(
            last_hidden_state=hidden_states,
            intermediate_hidden_states=intermediate,
            intermediate_logits=intermediate_logits,
            intermediate_reference_points=intermediate_reference_points,
            hidden_states=all_hidden_states,
            attentions=all_self_attns,
            cross_attentions=all_cross_attentions,
        )
class RTDetrV2FrozenBatchNorm2d(nn.Module):

num_classes,
    num_queries,
    class_embed,
    num_denoising_queries=100,
    label_noise_ratio=0.5,
    box_noise_scale=1.0,
):
    """
    Creates a contrastive denoising training group using ground-truth samples. It adds noise to labels and boxes.

Args:
        targets (`list[dict]`):
            The target objects, each containing 'class_labels' and 'boxes' for objects in an image.
        num_classes (`int`):
            Total number of classes in the dataset.
        num_queries (`int`):
            Number of query slots in the transformer.
        class_embed (`callable`):
            A function or a model layer to embed class labels.
        num_denoising_queries (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 100):
            Number of denoising queries.
        label_noise_ratio (`float`, *optional*, defaults to 0.5):
            Ratio of noise applied to labels.
        box_noise_scale (`float`, *optional*, defaults to 1.0):
            Scale of noise applied to bounding boxes.
    Returns:
        `tuple` comprising various elements:
        - **input_query_class** (`torch.FloatTensor`) --
          Class queries with applied label noise.
        - **input_query_bbox** (`torch.FloatTensor`) --
          Bounding box queries with applied box noise.
        - **attn_mask** (`torch.FloatTensor`) --
           Attention mask for separating denoising and reconstruction queries.
        - **denoising_meta_values** (`dict`) --
          Metadata including denoising positive indices, number of groups, and split sizes.
    """

if num_denoising_queries <= 0:
        return None, None, None, None

num_ground_truths = [len(t["class_labels"]) for t in targets]
    device = targets[0]["class_labels"].device

num_groups_denoising_queries = num_denoising_queries // max_gt_num
    num_groups_denoising_queries = 1 if num_groups_denoising_queries == 0 else num_groups_denoising_queries
    # pad gt to max_num of a batch
    batch_size = len(num_ground_truths)

input_query_class = torch.full([batch_size, max_gt_num], num_classes, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    input_query_bbox = torch.zeros([batch_size, max_gt_num, 4], device=device)
    pad_gt_mask = torch.zeros([batch_size, max_gt_num], dtype=torch.bool, device=device)

for i in range(batch_size):
        num_gt = num_ground_truths[i]
        if num_gt > 0:
            input_query_class[i, :num_gt] = targets[i]["class_labels"]
            input_query_bbox[i, :num_gt] = targets[i]["boxes"]
            pad_gt_mask[i, :num_gt] = 1
    # each group has positive and negative queries.
    input_query_class = input_query_class.tile([1, 2 * num_groups_denoising_queries])
    input_query_bbox = input_query_bbox.tile([1, 2 * num_groups_denoising_queries, 1])
    pad_gt_mask = pad_gt_mask.tile([1, 2 * num_groups_denoising_queries])
    # positive and negative mask
    negative_gt_mask = torch.zeros([batch_size, max_gt_num * 2, 1], device=device)
    negative_gt_mask[:, max_gt_num:] = 1
    negative_gt_mask = negative_gt_mask.tile([1, num_groups_denoising_queries, 1])
    positive_gt_mask = 1 - negative_gt_mask
    # contrastive denoising training positive index
    positive_gt_mask = positive_gt_mask.squeeze(-1) * pad_gt_mask
    denoise_positive_idx = torch.nonzero(positive_gt_mask)[:, 1]
    denoise_positive_idx = torch.split(
        denoise_positive_idx, [n * num_groups_denoising_queries for n in num_ground_truths]
    )
    # total denoising queries
    num_denoising_queries = torch_int(max_gt_num * 2 * num_groups_denoising_queries)

if label_noise_ratio > 0:
        mask = torch.rand_like(input_query_class, dtype=torch.float) < (label_noise_ratio * 0.5)
        # randomly put a new one here
        new_label = torch.randint_like(mask, 0, num_classes, dtype=input_query_class.dtype)
        input_query_class = torch.where(mask & pad_gt_mask, new_label, input_query_class)

if box_noise_scale > 0:
        known_bbox = center_to_corners_format(input_query_bbox)
        diff = torch.tile(input_query_bbox[..., 2:] * 0.5, [1, 1, 2]) * box_noise_scale
        rand_sign = torch.randint_like(input_query_bbox, 0, 2) * 2.0 - 1.0
        rand_part = torch.rand_like(input_query_bbox)
        rand_part = (rand_part + 1.0) * negative_gt_mask + rand_part * (1 - negative_gt_mask)
        rand_part *= rand_sign
        known_bbox += rand_part * diff
        known_bbox.clip_(min=0.0, max=1.0)
        input_query_bbox = corners_to_center_format(known_bbox)
        input_query_bbox = inverse_sigmoid(input_query_bbox)
input_query_class = class_embed(input_query_class)

target_size = num_denoising_queries + num_queries
    attn_mask = torch.full([target_size, target_size], 0, dtype=torch.float, device=device)
    # match query cannot see the reconstruction
    attn_mask[num_denoising_queries:, :num_denoising_queries] = -torch.inf

# reconstructions cannot see each other
    for i in range(num_groups_denoising_queries):
        idx_block_start = max_gt_num * 2 * i
        idx_block_end = max_gt_num * 2 * (i + 1)
        attn_mask[idx_block_start:idx_block_end, :idx_block_start] = -torch.inf
        attn_mask[idx_block_start:idx_block_end, idx_block_end:num_denoising_queries] = -torch.inf
return input_query_class, input_query_bbox, attn_mask, denoising_meta_values

    enc_topk_logits (`torch.FloatTensor` of shape `(batch_size, sequence_length, config.num_labels)`, *optional*, returned when `config.with_box_refine=True` and `config.two_stage=True`):

context.pr_body:
# What does this PR do?

As per the title. Until now, if a class was ever referenced in the modular file BEFORE being redefined in it later on in the file, it could match a class from another modeling file, thus adding wrong dependencies to the generated files.
This PR fixes it, by making sure all classes redefined in modular are removed from the dependency graph of another class if present (they will be added later on with their own dependencies)

So the order of class definition and class reference in modular files can now be arbitrary 🎉(even though to keep clean code, we always want classes to be defined before they are used somewhere, so that someone can read the file "naturally", it is sometimes not practical)

As an example, consider `modular_modernbert_decoder` which is being modified, where I previously had to use a check on string name instead of `isinstance(class)` because the 2 classes are defined afterwards in modular, and would thus bring erroneous dependencies.

@pytest.mark.parametrize('validate_json', [True, False])
def test_secretstr(validate_json):
    class Foobar(BaseModel):
        password: SecretStr
        empty_password: SecretStr

    if validate_json:
        f = Foobar.model_validate_json('{"password": "1234", "empty_password": ""}')
        with pytest.raises(ValidationError) as exc_info:
            Foobar.model_validate_json('{"password": 1234, "empty_password": null}')
    else:
        f = Foobar(password='1234', empty_password='')
        with pytest.raises(ValidationError) as exc_info:
            Foobar(password=1234, empty_password=None)

    assert exc_info.value.errors(include_url=False) == [
        {'type': 'string_type', 'loc': ('password',), 'msg': 'Input should be a valid string', 'input': 1234},
        {'type': 'string_type', 'loc': ('empty_password',), 'msg': 'Input should be a valid string', 'input': None},
    ]

    # Assert correct types.
    assert f.password.__class__.__name__ == 'SecretStr'
    assert f.empty_password.__class__.__name__ == 'SecretStr'

    # Assert str and repr are correct.
    assert str(f.password) == '**********'
    assert str(f.empty_password) == ''
    assert repr(f.password) == "SecretStr('**********')"
    assert repr(f.empty_password) == "SecretStr('')"
    assert len(f.password) == 4
    assert len(f.empty_password) == 0

    # Assert retrieval of secret value is correct
    assert f.password.get_secret_value() == '1234'
    assert f.empty_password.get_secret_value() == ''

feat(iwork): complete the parsing of Apple Pages documents (#4062)

* feat(iwork): recover character formatting and text boxes

Bold, italic, underline and strikethrough are now read from both container
generations. Which protobuf field carries which property was established by
correlating character style names against their property fields across three
real Apple documents: Emphasis and Bold set field 1, Italic field 2, Underline
and Link field 11, Strikethrough field 12. The iWork 09 stylesheets use the same
names with matching property maps, so the two readers check each other.
Properties with no Formatting equivalent, such as colour or capitalisation, are
ignored rather than approximated.

Pages applies character styles to parts of a paragraph rather than whole ones,
so a paragraph is now kept as runs. Where the runs differ it becomes an inline
group, as the Word and HTML backends do; where they agree it stays one item.

Text boxes are floating drawables, reached from TP.DocumentArchive through its
drawables field and the shape that owns the text. Following ownership matters:
scanning every TSWP.StorageArchive would also pick up headers, footers and
footnotes, which hang off other fields and are deliberately excluded.

Adds pages_iwork09_formatted.pages, which carries a real underlined run, since
the existing fixtures define character styles but never apply them.

Signed-off-by: Daniel Nguyen <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* fix(iwork): keep the spaces around a formatted run

Pages ends a character style mid-sentence, so a run boundary falls inside
a word gap rather than at one. Trimming every run glued the words on both
sides together: "the Keynote APXL file" came out as "APXLfile", and "on
the Internet" as "theInternet".

Whitespace is now trimmed once per paragraph instead of once per run, so
the boundary no longer takes the space with it.

Signed-off-by: Daniel Nguyen <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* feat(iwork): recover bulleted and numbered lists

Part of #4025.

A Pages storage keeps two more run tables next to the paragraph and
character style tables the backend already read: one holding a nesting
depth per paragraph, and one holding the list style in force. Reading
both is what makes lists recoverable without walking anything new.

The depth alone is not enough, and reading it that way is the mistake
worth naming: Pages leaves a list style in force over ordinary body text
as well, marking it with the built-in "None" style, and records depth 0
for a document that has no nesting at all. What decides the question is
the style's label type at the paragraph's depth — kNone for plain text,
kString for a bullet whose marker the style carries, kNumber for an
ordered list.

The same distinction exists in iWork '09, where an sf:liststyle holds one
sf:list-label-typeinfo per level and a paragraph names its own
sf:list-level, counting from one rather than from zero.

Consecutive items are gathered into one list group, and a deeper item
opens a nested group under it.

Verified against a genuine Pages 5 document containing a bulleted list,
whose three items come back as one group. The fixture in the tree defines
Apple's "Bullet" and "Numbered List" styles but applies neither, so the
tests check the style decoding against those real definitions, and check
the run-table path by repointing the fixture's own list-style run from
"None" to the "Bullet" style it already contains.

Signed-off-by: Daniel Nguyen <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* feat(iwork): recover inline images and place drawables in the flow

Part of #4025.

A U+FFFC in a Pages storage marks where a drawable is anchored, and the
storage's attachment table says which one. The character was being
stripped and the drawable never looked for, so an image was lost outright
and a table was appended after the body instead of appearing where the
author put it.

Following the attachment recovers both. An image resolves through the
package metadata, which maps a data identifier to a Data/ member of the
container; Pages names every rendition it knows of, including ones it
never wrote, so the renditions are tried in turn and a picture whose bytes
are absent still keeps its place. An iWork '09 image names its member
directly on sf:data, and its bytes are read the same way.

Content is therefore modelled as ordered blocks — paragraphs, tables and
pictures — rather than paragraphs with tables appended, which is what puts
the fixture's table between the two body paragraphs it sits between. The
'09 walk gained the same ordering, and stops descending into a table, so
cell text cannot reappear as body text.

Verified against a genuine Pages 5 document that anchors both an image and
a table inline: both come back in place, and the image bytes resolve
through the rendition the container actually holds.

Signed-off-by: Daniel Nguyen <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* feat(iwork): recover headers, footers and footnotes

Part of #4025.

Both generations were pruning page furniture and discarding it. It is
recovered now, labelled and placed in the furniture content layer — the
same treatment the Word backend gives a header and a footer — so it stays
out of the reading order by default but is there for callers that ask.

Headers and footers belong to the page master a stretch of the document
runs under rather than to the text, so the modern reader reaches them
through the body storage's page master table and the headers-and-footers
bundle each master names. Pages writes a first-page, an even-page and an
odd-page variant whether or not the author filled them in, and repeats
them per section, so identical text is emitted once. The '09 reader has
the same duplication to handle in sf:headers and sf:footers.

A footnote is anchored at one of the U+FFFC placeholders the text carries,
in a run table of the same shape as the attachment table, and the note it
names holds a storage of its own.

The '09 fixture carries a real header, a real footer and three real
footnotes, and they come back intact. Both modern fixtures name six header
and footer storages and leave every one of them empty, so the modern path
is tested by giving two of those storages text and by appending a footnote
table to the fixture's own body storage, leaving the rest of the graph as
Pages wrote it.

Signed-off-by: Daniel Nguyen <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* feat(iwork): recover comments

Part of #4025.

Comments were not merely missing from an iWork '09 document, they were
being emitted as body text: sf:annotations sits outside the body but the
walk that collected paragraphs did not know that, so every comment
appeared in the reading order as if the author had written it there.

They are now read as comments and put in the notes content layer, where
the Word backend puts them, and each is attached to the text it annotates:
an '09 annotation names the sf:annotation-field it targets, and a Pages 5
comment is recorded as a highlight over the words it is about, so the run
table gives the stretch of text rather than a character in it. A reply is
a comment in its own right, so a thread is followed as a chain, and each
is prefixed with its author the way the Word backend renders one.

Adds pages_iwork09_comments.pages, from the same Apache-licensed Tika
corpus as the other fixtures; it carries three real comments on three
different paragraphs. The modern path is tested by appending a comment
table to the fixture's own body storage, so the text, the styles and the
paragraph boundaries around it stay exactly as Pages wrote them.

Signed-off-by: Daniel Nguyen <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* feat(iwork): recover superscript, subscript and hyperlinks

Part of #4025.

Character styles carry more than the four flags already read. Field 10 of
a modern style, and sf:superscript in an '09 property map, both hold the
same three-valued setting — neither, raised, lowered — which is what
Formatting.script records.

Hyperlinks live somewhere else entirely. Pages calls one a smart field and
keeps it in a run table of its own, so a link and a character style are
independent boundaries and both have to cut the paragraph; a run is now
identified by the pair. An '09 link instead wraps the spans it covers, and
href is one of the few attributes iWork writes unqualified, so attributes
are looked up under either spelling.

The same lookup problem appears one level up: sf:style on a paragraph or a
span sometimes names a style's sf:ident and sometimes its sfa:ID, and only
the first was indexed, so any style referenced the other way silently
resolved to nothing. Both are indexed now, which is what makes the '09
fixture's link style resolve at all.

Page furniture goes through the same run assembly as body text rather than
being flattened to a string, so the URL in the fixture's third footnote
survives instead of being dropped on the way out.

Signed-off-by: Daniel Nguyen <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* feat(iwork): read tables saved by Pages 5.2 and later

Part of #4025.

Table support went in against a document Pages 5.0 wrote, and every
document written since stores its cells differently: the row's cell buffer
and its offsets moved to new fields, the offsets are scaled by four when
the row says so, and the packed cell gained a flags word that decides where
its value sits rather than fixing it at one offset. A reader that knows
only the older layout finds no cells and drops the whole table without
saying anything.

Both layouts are read now. The older fields are still written alongside the
new ones, so the new pair is preferred where it exists rather than taking
whichever is found first.

Recent Pages also stores a styled cell's text as rich text — a key into a
second value list whose entries point at a whole TSWP.StorageArchive —
rather than as a plain string, which is what the table in every current
template uses. Both value lists are read, including the segments a long one
spills into.

Verified against a genuine Pages document from 2018 whose table came back
empty before and now comes back with its header row and its item names. The
fixture in the tree predates the change, so its own tile is rewritten into
the new layout, with and without scaled offsets, over the model, geometry
and string list Pages wrote.

Signed-off-by: Daniel Nguyen <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* docs(iwork): describe what Apple Pages parsing now covers

Closes #4025.

The "What's new" entries in the README and the docs index said only that
Pages is parsed, and the usage docs still listed lists, headers, footers,
footnotes and comments as missing. Both now describe what is read, and the
supported-formats table lists it too.

The advanced-options section gains the content each generation yields, how
to include page furniture in an export, and what genuinely has no published
format — equations, charts and form controls — separated from what is
simply not read yet.

Signed-off-by: Daniel Nguyen <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* refactor(iwork): split the Pages backend into a model and two readers

The backend module had grown to 2644 lines and past the 1500-line limit the
repository enforces, with three unrelated things in it: what a Pages
document holds, how each of the two containers spells that, and how it
becomes a DoclingDocument.

They are separate modules now, which is also where the review of #3934
pointed:

- content: the model both generations read into, and the helpers that work
  on it — runs, paragraphs, lists, pictures, comments.
- pages_iwa: the Pages 5+ object graph, and only the message and field
  numbers as format knowledge.
- pages_xml: the iWork '09 sf: vocabulary.
- pages_backend: the container dispatch and the document assembly.

Each reader now exposes one read_content(), so the backend decides which
generation wrote the file and nothing else. No behaviour changes: every
Pages document available produces the same output, item for item, as
before the split.

Signed-off-by: Daniel Nguyen <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* fix(iwork): repair the license headers the merge left behind

Merging main brought in the license header hook from #4067. Resolving the
conflict in pages_backend.py kept the opening line of both sides, which put
the header inside the module docstring and left a second docstring opener
after it. The file stopped being valid Python, so ruff could not parse it
and the lint job failed on it rather than on anything it checks for.

The three modules the backend was split into were added after the hook ran
over the tree, so they had no header at all.

Signed-off-by: Daniel Nguyen <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* Update README.md

Co-authored-by: Cesar Berrospi Ramis <75900930+ceberam@users.noreply.github.com>
Signed-off-by: Nguyen Hoang Duong <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* Update docs/index.md

Co-authored-by: Cesar Berrospi Ramis <75900930+ceberam@users.noreply.github.com>

* Update tests/test_backend_iwork_pages.py

Co-authored-by: Cesar Berrospi Ramis <75900930+ceberam@users.noreply.github.com>

* Update docs/usage/supported_formats.md

Co-authored-by: Cesar Berrospi Ramis <75900930+ceberam@users.noreply.github.com>

* Update docling/backend/iwork/pages_iwa.py

Signed-off-by: Nguyen Hoang Duong <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* refactor(iwork): move the Pages backend alongside the other backends

Addresses review feedback on #4062.

`docling/backend` holds backend modules, so the backend itself belongs
there rather than inside a supporting package. `IWorkPagesDocumentBackend`
moves back to `docling/backend/iwork_backend.py`, which is also where the
Numbers and Keynote backends will go when they follow, matching how
`opendocument_backend.py` holds all three OpenDocument backends.

`docling/backend/iwork` keeps only what those backends are built from: the

The package no longer re-exports the backend, which would now be a cycle.

Signed-off-by: Daniel Nguyen <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* docs(iwork): trim the Pages section to its actionable options

Addresses review feedback on #4062.

advanced_options.md is for advanced conversion options, not for explaining
what Pages is or how each kind of content is parsed. Only two things there
are actually options a caller can act on: asking for the content layers
that page furniture and comments go into, and tuning the size limits on an
untrusted container. The section now covers those and nothing else, and
says the layer argument applies to any DoclingDocument rather than reading

The list label type constants also each carry their own line of
explanation, since a reader meeting LABEL_TYPE_NONE first had to find the
docstring three constants further down.

Signed-off-by: Daniel Nguyen <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* test(iwork): pin every Pages fixture against a stored groundtruth

Addresses review feedback on #4062.

Each fixture that converts now has its Markdown and its serialized

The two views are complementary. The Markdown is the reading order a

* refactor(iwork): finish the split the backend move left half-done

context.pr_body:
Hi maintainers this PR is to add further improvement for iwork pages mentioned in #4025 
Adds character formatting and text boxes.

## Character formatting

Bold, italic, underline and strikethrough are recovered in **both** container generations.

The obstacle was never the XML side; it was knowing which protobuf fields carry which property in the IWA container. That turned out to be answerable from real documents: a `TSWP.CharacterStyleArchive` carries a name, and correlating names with their property fields across three genuine Apple files settles it 

| Field | Property | Confirmed by styles named |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | bold | `Emphasis`, `Bold`, `Red Bold` |
| 2 | italic | `Italic` |
| 11 | underline | `Underline`, `Link` |
| 12 | strikethrough | `Strikethrough` |

The same names appear in the iWork '09 stylesheets with matching property maps, so the two readers were checked against each other rather than against my assumptions. Properties with no `Formatting` equivalent, colour, font,
capitalisation are all ignored rather than approximated.

### Paragraphs are now runs

Pages applies character styles to arbitrary stretches of a paragraph, not to whole paragraphs: in every fixture I examined, the underline covers part of a sentence. `TextItem` carries a single `Formatting`, so a paragraph whose runs differ becomes an inline group of items, the same shape the Word and HTML backends produce. A paragraph whose runs agree stays a single item.

A test asserts both halves: the underlined run keeps its formatting, and the formatting does not bleed onto the text around it.

## Text boxes

Text boxes are floating drawables rather than body content, so they are reached
by ownership:

```
TP.DocumentArchive → drawables → TSWP.ShapeInfoArchive → TSWP.StorageArchive
```

Scanning every `TSWP.StorageArchive` would be simpler and is the obvious shortcut. It is also wrong: headers, footers and footnotes are storages too, and #4031 deliberately excluded them after finding they leaked into the body flow.
Following the drawables field preserves that distinction, and the whole Tika corpus was re-checked for leakage.

iWork '09 keeps text boxes in the body flow, so they already appeared there; this affects the modern container only and narrows the gap between the readers.


## Testing

42 tests, all model-free and backed by genuine Apple output from the Apache Tika corpus (Apache-2.0). One fixture is added:
`pages_iwork09_formatted.pages`, which carries a real underlined run.

New coverage: character formatting is recovered and stays confined to its run; the IWA property-field mapping is checked against the styles the fixture defines; text box content is extracted; and text boxes are reached by ownership
rather than by scanning every storage.

The backend was also run across every Pages document in the corpus, confirming no page furniture leaks in and nothing else changed.

`ruff format --check`, `ruff check`, `ty check` and `tach check` are clean, with no new `ty` diagnostics.

**Checklist:**

- [x] Documentation has been updated, if necessary.
- [x] Examples have been added, if necessary.
- [x] Tests have been added, if necessary.
issue_titles: Complete the parsing of iWork Pages
issue_bodies:
The PR #3934 drafted a first declarative backend, `IWorkPagesDocumentBackend`, to parse Apple's iWork Pages documents. The backend needs some improvements to pair the capabilities of similar backend parsers like `MsWordDocumentBackend` for Word documents.

Just drop a line if you're interested in resolving this issue. Make sure to follow the [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/docling-project/docling/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). If leveraging AI assistants, ensure that the code standards described in [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/docling-project/docling/blob/main/AGENTS.md) are enabled.

## Features

The task should cover:

- comments in the initial PR that could not be addressed on time (see unresolved conversations in #3934 and first bullet of https://github.com/docling-project/docling/pull/3934#pullrequestreview-4959483218
- missing features of `IWorkPagesDocumentBackend` (see below)
- documentation of the feature in README (_What's new_), [index.md](https://github.com/docling-project/docling/blob/main/docs/index.md), and [supported_formats.md](https://github.com/docling-project/docling/blob/main/docs/usage/supported_formats.md)


## Missing features

### ✅ Feasible — paragraph/character style runs live in the *same archive already being read*

The `TSWP.StorageArchive` that the backend already locates contains not just the raw text (field 3) but also:

- **Field 5 — paragraph style runs**: byte ranges → paragraph style reference. Each paragraph style carries a style *name* (`"Heading 1"`…`"Heading 6"`, `"Title"`, `"Body"`, etc.), giving headings for free.
- **Field 6 — character style runs**: byte ranges → character style reference. Each character style archive has boolean fields for **bold, italic, underline, strikethrough**, and a script field for **superscript/subscript**. These map directly to Docling's `Formatting` dataclass used by `MsWordDocumentBackend._get_format_from_run()`.

These require decoding two more field arrays from the archive that is already decompressed in memory — no new object-graph walking needed.

### 🟡 Partial / significant effort — requires walking *additional* object references

- **Numbered & bullet lists**: The paragraph style run references a list style object with a nesting level and list type (bullet/ordered). Requires following the list style reference and tracking indent depth.
- **Tables**: Stored in `TST.TableModelArchive` objects (message type ~6001) referenced from the document's drawable list. Requires walking the drawable object graph, extracting row/col counts and cell text from `TST.TableDataStore`. The `_handle_tables()` equivalent would need to be written.
- **Text boxes**: Currently missed because only one `TSWP.StorageArchive` is followed (the body). Iterating *all* `TSWP.StorageArchive` objects across all `.iwa` files would pick up text boxes; distinguishing body vs. text-box storages needs the drawable reference graph.
- **Inline images**: Image bytes sit in `Data/` members of the ZIP, referenced from `TP.DrawableArchive` objects. Requires following drawable references and reading ZIP members by path.
- **Headers & footers, footnotes, comments**: All use the same attachment/anchor mechanism. Footnote anchors are U+FFFC characters in the text that the current code silently strips (`_clean()`). Following the attachment object from each U+FFFC can recover footnote/comment text.

### 🔴 Blocked — out of scope

- **Mathematical equations**: Pages uses a proprietary equation format with no published schema. The Word backend's OMML→LaTeX pipeline has no equivalent.
- **Charts**: Stored in deeply nested `TSD.*Archive` objects; even community tools (libetonyek, iwa2csv) have not fully mapped them.
- **Checkboxes / form controls**: Pages has no equivalent of DOCX content controls.


> **Key insight**: Almost every feasible feature requires either (a) reading the paragraph/character style run arrays already present in the `TSWP.StorageArchive` the backend already decompresses, or (b) walking additional object references that hang off the same document object. The IWA infrastructure (`iter_objects` / `read_fields` / `read_reference`) is already in place; it is the per-feature decoding logic that is missing.

The goal of this module (`advanced_options.md`) is to explain advanced conversion options, rather than a tutorial on what Pages is and how each section has been parsed. The only two things that are actually advanced and actionable for a user are how to include furniture in an export and how to tune the size limits. Can you please refactor the _Convert Apple Pages documents_ accordingly?

What about this? (it's just an idea)

### Apple Pages options

Headers, footers and footnotes go into the `furniture` content layer, and
comments into `notes`, so they stay out of the reading order by default. To
include them in an export, pass the extra layers explicitly (this applies to
any `DoclingDocument`, not just Pages):

```python
from docling_core.types.doc import ContentLayer
from docling.document_converter import DocumentConverter

doc = DocumentConverter().convert("report.pages").document
print(doc.export_to_markdown(included_content_layers={ContentLayer.BODY, ContentLayer.FURNITURE}))
```

The container is untrusted input, so size limits apply. They can be tuned with
`IWorkBackendOptions`:

```python
from docling.datamodel.backend_options import IWorkBackendOptions
from docling.datamodel.base_models import InputFormat
from docling.document_converter import DocumentConverter, IWorkPagesFormatOption

doc_converter = DocumentConverter(
    format_options={
        InputFormat.IWORK_PAGES: IWorkPagesFormatOption(
            backend_options=IWorkBackendOptions(max_total_bytes=50 * 1024 * 1024)
        )
    }
)

review_comments.body:
Hi Dr @ceberam sorry for this. It is not intentional and it's a leak

That paragraph is iWork '09 template placeholder text ("greeked" pseudo-English that Pages shows until the author types over it), which is why we cant see in the document. This PR already prunes `sf:ghost-text` for exactly this reason, but misses its sibling `sf:ghost-text-ref`: a template defines each placeholder once, and every paragraph that reuses it holds a `ghost-text-ref` that names the original by `sfa:IDREF` but carries its own inline copy of the text. Pruning only the first tag let the copy through.

This also affects all three '09 fixtures, not just `pages_iwork09.pages`. Each has 7 `sf:ghost-text` and 2 `sf:ghost-text-ref` elements, one of the latter carrying that paragraph so they're the same source document saved three ways.

I'll open a PR (#4170) to resolved this right away. Thank you very much for your review

def test_vlm_incomplete_split_keeps_single_file(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    main = tmp_path / "model.F16.gguf"
    main.write_bytes(b"m" * 2_000_001)
    monkeypatch.setattr(save_mod, "_find_llama_gguf_split", lambda _: "splitter")

    def incomplete_run(args, **kwargs):
        prefix = Path(args[-1])
        (prefix.parent / f"{prefix.name}-00001-of-00002.gguf").write_bytes(b"one")
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(args, 0, stdout = "ok", stderr = "")

    monkeypatch.setattr(save_mod.subprocess, "run", incomplete_run)

    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match = "incomplete shard set"):
        save_mod._split_main_gguf([str(main)], "1MB", "quantizer")
    assert main.exists()

context.pr_body:
Remove the GGUF shard controls introduced by #6107. This removes the export toggles, split-folder naming, “Sharded · N parts” labels, API/MCP fields, and saving helpers, and restores the original 50GB converter limit.

Preserve existing split-GGUF discovery and loading, custom output folders, private Hub uploads, and independent later fixes.

## Checks

- 230 focused Python tests and 12 frontend export tests passed.
- Frontend production build, Ruff, and API schema checks passed.
